# Vector writing format

<!-- Generated by kition-sdk tools/writing-format.mjs from the Vector engine and agent/guide.md. Regenerate it; do not edit it by hand. -->

What a model or a script writes to make or change a Vector document: the run syntax, every
command and its parameters, the value lists and the defaults the engine states, and worked examples.
It is made from the command catalogue of the Vector engine 0.3.21. Read
[`agent/guide.md`](../agent/guide.md) first: it says how to address things, the workflow, and the
pitfalls.

## Syntax

Changes are steps of `vector_run`; each step is one command with its parameters as JSON:

```json
vector_run { "path": "<file>", "steps": [{ "command": "<command id>", "params": { … } }] }
```

A run is one step in the document's history. `vector_commands` finds commands by words; the
lists below are the whole catalogue. A parameter marked required must be given; a parameter left out
takes the engine's default (listed where the engine states one). Commands marked (reads) answer
without changing the document.

| `css.selection` | `rasterize` | `false` |
| `css.selection` | `unnamed` | `true` |
| `print.presets.import` | `replace` | `false` |
| `object.vectorHalftone` | `clip` | `true` |
| `object.vectorHalftone` | `keepOriginal` | `false` |
| `perspective.presets.import` | `replace` | `false` |

## Commands

720 commands, by menu.

### File

- `file.new` (writes): Creates a new document and makes it active, optionally from a named preset with its own size, units, orientation, artboards, bleed and colour mode; answers the new document's index. Use document.open for an existing file.
  - `artboardLayout` object, default: all in one row
  - `artboards` integer, 1–1000
  - `backgroundContents` string, one of `transparent` | `white`, a white artboard background, not an object
  - `bleed` number or array or object
  - `colorMode` string, one of `rgb` | `cmyk`, a CMYK document starts with CMYK swatches and stores the colours applied to it as CMYK
  - `created` number or null
  - `height` number, default `792`, points
  - `name` string
  - `orientation` string, one of `portrait` | `landscape`, swaps width and height to match
  - `preset` string
  - `previewMode` string, one of `default` | `pixel` | `overprint`, overprint turns Overprint Preview on, pixel Pixel Preview in the app; default leaves both
  - `rasterEffectsPpi` integer, one of `72` | `150` | `300`, 1–2400
  - `title` string
  - `units` string, one of `Pixels` | `Points` | `Picas` | `Inches` | `Millimeters` | `Centimeters` | `Feet` | `Yards` | `Meters` | `Feet & Inches`, default: prefs unitsGeneral, as print presets; screen presets: Pixels
  - `width` number, points; default 612|"210 mm"
- `file.close` (writes): Closes the document at index (default the active one) without saving; use document.save first to keep changes.
  - `index` integer, a position counted from 0 (the first is 0)
- `document.exportSelection` (reads): Exports only the selected objects, cropped to their bounds, as PNG, JPEG, WebP, SVG or PDF; answers the file or its data with the bounds.
  - `format` string, one of `png` | `jpg` | `webp` | `svg` | `svgz` | `pdf`, default: from the extension, else png
  - `path` file
  - `scale` integer, default `1`
- `document.exportForOffice` (reads): Writes one artboard as a PNG at a chosen resolution for office documents and slides, or answers its data when no path is given.
  - `artboard` integer, default `0`
  - `path` file
  - `ppi` integer, default `150`, 72, 150, 300… pixels per inch
  - `transparent` boolean, default `false`, else on white
- `file.saveAs` (writes): Saves the document to a new path and format, after which the document takes that path, name and format (a template is always a copy).
  - `format` string, one of `kvector` | `template` | `pdf` | `svg` | `svgz` | `ai`, default: the path's extension, else the document's own
  - `modified` number or null
  - `options` object
  - `path` file
  - `svg` object
- `file.saveCopy` (reads): Writes a copy of the document to path in a format while the document keeps its own path, title and modified state.
  - `format` string, one of `kvector` | `template` | `pdf` | `svg` | `svgz` | `ai`
  - `options` object
  - `path` file
- `file.saveAsTemplate` (writes): Writes the document as a native template that opens as a new untitled document; the document itself is unchanged.
  - `compress` boolean
  - `path` file
  - `version` integer
- `file.newFromTemplate` (writes): Opens a template (or any readable file) as a new untitled document, leaving the template file untouched.
  - `path` file
- `file.revert` (writes): Discards unsaved changes by reloading the document's saved file into the same tab and clearing its history; only for saved, modified documents. No parameters.
- `file.closeAll` (writes): Closes every open document without saving; answers how many closed. No parameters.
- `file.info` (writes): Sets the document's File Info metadata (title, author, description, keywords, rating, copyright) in one undo step.
  - `author` string
  - `authorTitle` string
  - `copyrightNotice` string
  - `copyrightStatus` string, one of `unknown` | `copyrighted` | `publicDomain`
  - `copyrightUrl` string
  - `description` string
  - `keywords` array or string
  - `rating` integer
  - `title` string
- `file.place` (writes): Places a file (image, PDF page, document or text) into the document at a position or rect, linked or embedded; answers the placed object.
  - `at` number[]
  - `crop` string, one of `crop` | `bounding` | `art` | `trim` | `bleed` | `media`, clipped to that page or artboard, default; the art's bounds; a PDF page's boxes
  - `dxf` object, a .dxf drawing: fit fills the artboard under at, else the first; fitted or uncentred art lands with its drawing's artboard on that artboard, else it is centred on at
  - `link` boolean, default `true`, a raster image keeps its file's path; a Kition Vector document at path becomes one locked placed document showing artboard `page`, linked to the file and read again when it changes (links.update; saving it in this app updates it at once), drawn as vectors in every output; false: an editable copy of its art, as from dataBase64; other files are embedded
  - `page` integer, default `1`, PDF/.ai page, or a native document's artboard
  - `password` string
  - `rect` number[]
  - `replace` boolean, default `false`, swap the one selected object, keeping its stacking place and transform; no at/rect
  - `template` boolean, default `false`, onto a new locked template layer below the current layer
  - `text` object, UTF-8, or UTF-16 with a byte-order mark; other bytes as the platform's 8-bit set; the platform's 8-bit set; Windows-1252; Mac Roman; each block of lines becomes one paragraph; blank lines end paragraphs; drop blank lines; runs of n ≥ 2 spaces become a tab; a .txt file, placed as area type filling rect, the replaced object's bounds, or else the artboard less a 36 pt margin

### (no menu)

- `document.activate` (reads): Makes the open document at index the active one, so later commands act on it.
  - `index` integer, a position counted from 0 (the first is 0)
- `document.inspect` (reads): Answers the active document's layer tree, artboards, selection and history; depth and childLimit slice large trees. Start here before editing, and use document.node for one object.
  - `childLimit` integer
  - `depth` integer
- `document.node` (reads): Answers one object by id: its kind, geometry, paint and children; summary gives a compact form, depth and childLimit bound the children shown.
  - `childLimit` integer
  - `depth` integer
  - `id` integer or string, an id
  - `summary` boolean
- `document.find` (reads): Searches the document's objects by Layers panel name, kind or text content and answers the matches with their ids and paths; limit 0 only counts.
  - `Path` string
  - `kind` string
  - `limit` integer
  - `name` string
  - `text` string
- `document.json` (reads): Answers the complete document model as JSON; large, so prefer document.inspect or document.node unless you need everything. No parameters.
- `edit.duplicate` (writes): Duplicates the selection in place, optionally offset by dx/dy, and selects the copies.
  - `dx` number
  - `dy` number
- `clipboard.exportSvg` (reads): Answers the clipboard's objects as standalone SVG markup, or null when the clipboard is empty; the document is unchanged. No parameters.
- `clipboard.importSvg` (reads): Replaces the kit's clipboard with the objects of SVG markup or SVG/SVGZ bytes, centred on center; run edit.pasteInPlace afterwards to place them.
  - `center` number[]
  - `dataBase64` string, SVG or SVGZ bytes; one of several alternative parameters
  - `svg` string
- `clipboard.conflicts` (reads): Answers the global or spot swatches on the clipboard whose names the active document gives another colour, so you can pass swatchConflict to a paste. No parameters.
- `clipboard.exportPng` (reads): Answers the clipboard's objects as a PNG cropped to their visual bounds with a transparent background, at scale pixels per point.
  - `scale` integer, default `1`, pixels per point, up to 64
- `clipboard.exportPdf` (reads): Answers the clipboard's objects as a one-page PDF sized to their visual bounds, or null when the clipboard is empty. No parameters.
- `clipboard.exportText` (reads): Answers the copied type objects' text, one object per line, or null unless every copied object is type. No parameters.
- `clipboard.flavours` (reads): Answers the MIME types Copy offers other applications for the current clipboard, best first, according to the clipboard preferences. No parameters.
- `clipboard.importImage` (reads): Replaces the kit's clipboard with an embedded image from PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, TIFF or BMP bytes at its physical size; run edit.paste afterwards.
  - `center` number[]
  - `dataBase64` string, PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, TIFF or BMP bytes
  - `mime` string
- `clipboard.importText` (reads): Replaces the kit's clipboard with point text of the given text in the default type style; run edit.paste afterwards.
  - `center` number[]
  - `text` string
- `clipboard.importPdf` (reads): Replaces the kit's clipboard with the objects of one page of a PDF (with its images and swatches); run edit.paste afterwards.
  - `center` number[]
  - `dataBase64` string
  - `page` integer, default `1`
  - `password` string
- `clipboard.importEmf` (reads): Replaces the kit's clipboard with the paths, images and type of an EMF or WMF picture; unsupported records are skipped with a warning. Run edit.paste afterwards.
  - `center` number[]
  - `dataBase64` string, EMF or WMF bytes
- `recolor.colors` (reads): Answers the unique colours the selection uses (fills, strokes, gradient stops, text, meshes, pattern tiles) with their keys, hex values and use counts, most used first; feed the keys to recolor.apply. No parameters.
- `recolor.reduce` (reads): Groups the selection's colours into a given number of rows of similar colours and answers the proposed map, without changing anything; pass the map to recolor.apply.
  - `colors` integer, rows; default: one per colour, with the tints of a global swatch in its row
  - `limitTo` string
  - `method` string, one of `exact` | `preserveTints` | `scaleTints` | `tintsShades` | `hueShift`
  - `preserve` object, left out of the rows
- `recolor.randomize` (reads): Answers a recolour map with the rows' new colours shuffled or their saturation and brightness randomised (seeded), without changing the document; pass it to recolor.apply.
  - `map` array or object
  - `order` boolean, default `true`, shuffle the new colours among the rows that aren't excluded
  - `saturationBrightness` boolean, default `false`, random saturation and brightness, hue kept
  - `seed` integer, default `0`
- `document.open` (writes): Opens a file by path or from base64 bytes (native, SVG, PDF, AI, EPS, DXF, images and more) as a new active document; PDF options pick pages, the box and how text comes in.
  - `path` file
- `document.serialize` (reads): Answers the active document as file data in a format (native by default, SVG, PDF, raster and more) without writing a file or changing the document.
  - `format` string, one of `kvector` | `template` | `svg` | `svgz` | `pdf` | `png` | `jpg` | `webp` | `gif` | `png8` | `txt` | `dxf` | `eps` | `emf` | `wmf` | `tiff` | `bmp` | `tga` | `psd`, default
  - `selectedOnly` boolean, default `false`, the selected objects alone, in their layers
- `document.export` (reads): Writes the document, its selection or chosen artboards to a file in a format (SVG, PDF, PNG, JPEG, TIFF, PSD, DXF, EPS and more) with that format's options, or answers the data when no path is given. Never changes the document's own path.
  - `antiAlias` string, one of `none` | `art` | `type`, default; text snapped to pixels
  - `artboard` integer, default `0`
  - `artboards` array
  - `background` string
  - `bmp` object
  - `byteOrder` string, one of `little` | `big`
  - `colorModel` string, one of `rgb` | `cmyk` | `gray`
  - `depth` integer, default `24`, 1 black and white, 4|8 a palette by reduction and dither, 16, 24, 32 with alpha
  - `dither` string, one of `none` | `diffusion` | `pattern` | `noise`, default
  - `ditherAmount` integer, default `100`
  - `embedIcc` boolean, default `true`
  - `encoding` string, one of `utf8` | `utf16`, with a byte order mark
  - `fileFormat` string, one of `windows` | `os2`, 1, 4, 8 or 24 bits
  - `flipRows` boolean, default `false`, top-down rows
  - `format` string, one of `svg` | `svgz` | `pdf` | `png` | `jpg` | `webp` | `gif` | `png8` | `txt` | `dxf` | `eps` | `emf` | `wmf` | `tiff` | `bmp` | `tga` | `psd` | `kvector` | `template`, default: from the path's extension, else png; png8 writes an indexed .png
  - `hiddenLayers` boolean, default `false`, hidden layers and objects written hidden instead of left out
  - `imageMap` string, one of `none` | `client` | `server`, an HTML or NCSA map of the objects with a URL, written as <stem>.html / <stem>.map
  - `interlaced` boolean
  - `jpg` object
  - `layers` boolean, default `true`, each top-level layer a pixel layer with its opacity and blend mode; a background colour is a Background layer; false: one flat image, on white
  - `lineEndings` string, one of `lf` | `crlf`
  - `lzw` boolean, default `true`
  - `matte` string
  - `maxEditability` boolean, default `false`, layers and sublayers become groups, each object a layer named as in the Layers panel, text by its text; clipping, masked or knockout layers stay one layer
  - `method` string, one of `baseline` | `optimized` | `progressive`
  - `path` file
  - `psd` object
  - `range` string, one of `1-3, 5` | `all`, 1-based; PDF writes one page per artboard, default all; SVG writes one file per artboard, {stem}-{artboard}.svg; raster formats write one artboard
  - `raster` object
  - `reduction` string, one of `perceptual` | `selective` | `adaptive` | `web` | `blackWhite` | `gray`, default
  - `rle` boolean, default `false`, 4 and 8 bits, windows
  - `scale` integer, default `1`, pixels per point
  - `scans` integer, default `3`, 3–5, progressive
  - `selectedOnly` boolean, default `false`, the selected objects alone, in their layers
  - `selectionOnly` boolean
  - `tga` object
  - `tiff` object
  - `transparency` boolean, default `true`
  - `txt` object
  - `useArtboards` string, one of `true` | `false`, raster: one file per chosen artboard, default all, {stem}-{artboard}.{ext}; pdf: every page; pdf/raster: the bounds of the visible art; SVG has it as an SVG option
  - `webp` object
- `command.batch` (writes): Runs a list of commands as one undo step and stops at the first error, rolling everything back; use it for multi-step edits that must succeed together.
  - `commands` object[], [{command, params}]
  - `label` string
- `document.formats` (reads): Answers every file format the kit can open or write with its extensions and options, plus formats it cannot handle with what to use instead. No parameters.
- `document.pdfInfo` (reads): Answers a PDF's page count, page sizes and boxes, and optionally a thumbnail, without opening it; also says whether a password is needed.
  - `path` file
- `document.exportSettings` (reads): Answers the Export for Screens settings the document last exported with, or {} when it never was. No parameters.
- `document.save` (writes): Saves the document to its own file or to path in a format (native, template, PDF, SVG, AI) with that format's options; without a known path it answers the data and stays modified.
  - `embedProfiles` boolean, default `true`, carry the ICC profiles loaded from files that the document is tagged with; opening the file installs them where missing
  - `format` string, one of `kvector` | `template` | `pdf` | `svg` | `svgz` | `ai`, default: the path's extension, else the document's own format
  - `includeLinked` boolean, default `false`, keep linked files' own pixels, not just their previews; they stay linked
  - `modified` number or null
  - `native` object
  - `options` object
  - `path` file
  - `pdfCompatible` boolean
  - `svg` object, SVG options may also be given flat; an SVG save keeps hidden layers, display:none, unless hiddenLayers is false
  - `version` integer, default `3`, 2 or 1: for older Kition Vector versions, never compressed
- `file.formatOptions` (reads): Answers a writable format's options with their types, defaults and the values the document last saved with, plus the formats Save As offers.
  - `format` string
- `shape.rectangle` (writes): Draws a rectangle at x, y with width and height (optional corner radius and rotation about its centre) in the current layer with the current paint; answers its id.
  - `height` number
  - `radius` number, points
  - `rotation` number, degrees; about centre
  - `width` number
  - `x` number
  - `y` number
- `shape.ellipse` (writes): Draws an ellipse in the box x, y, width, height (optional rotation) with the current paint; answers its id.
  - `height` number
  - `rotation` number, degrees; about centre
  - `width` number
  - `x` number
  - `y` number
- `shape.polygon` (writes): Draws a regular polygon with a centre, radius and number of sides; answers its id.
  - `cx` number
  - `cy` number
  - `radius` number
  - `rotation` number, degrees
- `shape.star` (writes): Draws a star with a centre, outer and inner radii and a number of points; answers its id.
  - `cx` number
  - `cy` number
  - `radius1` number
  - `radius2` number
  - `rotation` number, degrees
- `shape.flare` (writes): Draws a lens flare (centre, halo, rays and rings) with the Flare tool's options; answers its id.
  - `cx` number
  - `cy` number
  - `seed` integer
  - `x2` number
  - `y2` number, ring end; else pathLength at direction
- `shape.line` (writes): Draws a straight line segment from x1, y1 to x2, y2 with the current stroke; answers its id.
  - `x1` number
  - `x2` number
  - `y1` number
  - `y2` number
- `shape.spiral` (writes): Draws a spiral with a centre, radius, decay and number of segments; answers its id.
  - `clockwise` boolean
  - `cx` number
  - `cy` number
  - `radius` number
- `shape.arc` (writes): Draws an arc from x1, y1 to x2, y2, open or closed; answers its id.
  - `closed` boolean
  - `x1` number
  - `x2` number
  - `y1` number
  - `y2` number
- `shape.rectangularGrid` (writes): Draws a rectangular grid of rows and columns in a box as one group; answers its id.
  - `height` number
  - `width` number
  - `x` number
  - `y` number
- `shape.polarGrid` (writes): Draws a polar grid of concentric and radial dividers in a box as one group; answers its id.
  - `height` number
  - `width` number
  - `x` number
  - `y` number
- `path.create` (writes): Creates a path from anchors with optional in/out handles, or from SVG path data, open or closed, with the current paint; answers its id.
  - `anchors` object[]
  - `closed` boolean
  - `d` string
- `view.drawMode` (reads): Sets where new objects go: drawn normally, behind the selection, or inside the one selected path (no mode cycles through them).
  - `mode` string, one of `normal` | `behind` | `inside`
- `text.create` (writes): Creates point or area type at x, y with text, size, font, colour and alignment options; answers its id. Use text.setText to change existing type.
  - `area` object, {width, height, fit?: none|autoHeight|shrinkText, fitMinPercent?}
  - `charAlign` string, one of `romanBaseline` | `emBoxTop` | `emBoxCenter` | `emBoxBottom` | `icfTop` | `icfBottom`, default: emBoxTop and emBoxCenter while the interface is in Japanese, else romanBaseline
  - `color` string
  - `font` string
  - `leadingModel` string, one of `romanBaseline` | `emBoxTop`
  - `placeholder` boolean, fill it with placeholder text instead, as the Type tools do with prefs placeholderText
  - `size` number, points
  - `style` string
  - `text` string
  - `vertical` boolean, default `false`
  - `x` number
  - `y` number
- `object.transform` (writes): Applies an affine matrix to the selection or ids, optionally as a copy and with strokes, corners, type areas and patterns scaling or not.
  - `copy` boolean
  - `corners` boolean
  - `ids` array
  - `matrix` number[], [a, b, c, d, e, f]
  - `patterns` boolean, Transform Patterns: pattern fills and strokes transform with the art; default: prefs transformPatternTiles
  - `strokes` boolean
  - `typeAreas` boolean
- `object.nudge` (writes): Nudges the selected anchors, else objects, else ruler guides by one keyboard increment in a direction (ten with big), as the arrow keys do.
  - `big` boolean, ×10
  - `copy` boolean
  - `dx` integer, one of `-1` | `0` | `1`
  - `dy` integer, one of `-1` | `0` | `1`
- `object.isolate` (reads): Enters isolation mode on the group or object id so later edits stay inside it; the document is unchanged.
  - `id` integer or string, an id
- `object.exitIsolation` (reads): Leaves isolation mode so edits apply to the whole document again; the document is unchanged. No parameters.
- `object.setProps` (writes): Sets object properties on ids or the selection: name, visibility, lock, opacity, blend mode, isolation, knockout and custom data attributes.
  - `blend` string
  - `data` object, {key: "value" | null (removes it)} (the object's own data, SVG data-* attributes: {pivot: "100,180"} is data-pivot; document.node → attrs.data); removes it; the object's own data, SVG data-* attributes: {pivot: "100,180"} is data-pivot; document.node → attrs.data
  - `isolate` boolean
  - `knockout` string or boolean
  - `knockoutShape` boolean
  - `locked` boolean
  - `name` string
  - `opacity` integer, 0 to 100
  - `visible` boolean
- `object.setBounds` (writes): Sets the selection's position and size as the Transform panel does, about one of nine reference points, optionally keeping proportions and scaling strokes and corners.
  - `corners` boolean
  - `height` number
  - `proportional` boolean
  - `reference` integer, 0 to 8; 9-point grid
  - `strokes` boolean
  - `width` number
  - `x` number
  - `y` number
- `object.setLiveShape` (writes): Edits live shape properties of the selected or given shapes: corner radius and kind per corner, polygon sides and angle, pie start and end angles.
  - `corners` array
  - `id` integer or string, an id
  - `ids` array
  - `invertPie` boolean, default `true`, swaps them: the other part of the ellipse
  - `items` object[], several objects, each with its own corners, in place of ids and corners: the canvas's corner widgets across a selection
  - `kind` string, one of `round` | `invertedRound` | `chamfer`
  - `makeSidesEqual` boolean, default `true`, a polygon scaled unevenly: drops the uneven scale and shear, keeping its centre, angle and mean radius
  - `pieEnd` number, degrees; an ellipse's pie, counterclockwise from 3 o'clock; 0 to 360 is the whole ellipse
  - `pieStart` number
  - `polygonAngle` number, degrees; counterclockwise from its first vertex straight up
  - `polygonRadius` number, points; centre to vertex
  - `radius` number, points
  - `sideLength` number, points; sets the radius
  - `sides` integer
- `path.appendAnchor` (writes): Appends an anchor with optional handles to the end of the last open subpath of path id, as the Pen tool does.
  - `id` integer or string, an id
  - `in` number[]
  - `out` number[]
  - `x` number
  - `y` number
- `path.close` (writes): Closes the last open subpath of path id, optionally setting the handle into its first anchor.
  - `id` integer or string, an id
  - `in` number[], handle into the first anchor
  - `independent` boolean
- `path.moveAnchors` (writes): Moves the direct-selected anchors by dx, dy (whole paths when fully selected).
  - `dx` number
  - `dy` number
- `path.setHandle` (writes): Moves the in or out direction handle of one anchor of path id to x, y, optionally breaking the handles' symmetry.
  - `anchor` integer
  - `id` integer or string, an id
  - `independent` boolean
  - `subpath` integer
  - `which` string, one of `in` | `out`
  - `x` number
  - `y` number
- `path.setAnchors` (writes): Replaces the whole geometry of path id with the given subpaths of anchors and handles.
  - `id` integer or string, an id
  - `subpaths` object[], [{anchors: [{x,y,in?,out?}], closed}]
- `path.convertAnchors` (writes): Converts the direct-selected anchors to corner points (handles retracted) or smooth points in one undo step.
  - `to` string, one of `corner` | `smooth`
- `path.deleteAnchors` (writes): Deletes the direct-selected anchors and their segments, opening closed paths at those points. No parameters.
- `path.reshape` (writes): Drags path id at a point by dx, dy as the Reshape tool does, with nearby anchors following on a smooth falloff.
  - `dx` number
  - `dy` number
  - `id` integer or string, an id
  - `radius` number
  - `x` number
  - `y` number
- `path.insertAnchor` (writes): Inserts an anchor on segment segment of subpath subpath of path id at parameter t without changing the path's shape.
  - `id` integer or string, an id
  - `segment` integer
  - `subpath` integer
  - `t` number, 0 to 1
- `path.cutAtAnchors` (writes): Cuts the paths at their direct-selected anchors, opening closed paths and splitting open ones; answers the ids of the pieces. No parameters.
- `select.set` (reads): Replaces the selection with the objects ids and answers the resulting selection; most editing commands then act on it.
  - `ids` array
- `select.add` (reads): Adds the objects ids to the selection and answers the resulting selection.
  - `ids` array
- `select.toggle` (reads): Toggles each of the objects id or ids in or out of the selection and answers the resulting selection.
  - `id` integer or string, an id
- `select.key` (reads): Makes one selected object the key object that Align aligns to and Distribute Spacing spaces from; no id clears it.
  - `id` integer
- `select.anchors` (reads): Sets, adds or toggles the direct selection of anchors (subpath and anchor indices) on path id.
  - `anchors` array
  - `id` integer or string, an id
  - `mode` string, one of `set` | `add` | `toggle`
- `select.anchorsMany` (reads): Sets, adds, toggles or subtracts direct-selected anchors on several paths at once.
  - `items` object[], [{id, anchors}]
  - `mode` string, one of `set` | `add` | `toggle` | `subtract`, set by default; add: true is mode add
- `select.magicWand` (reads): Selects objects similar to object id by the Magic Wand settings (fill, stroke, weight, opacity, blend), replacing, adding to or subtracting from the selection; answers the count.
  - `id` integer or string, an id
  - `mode` string, one of `set` | `add` | `subtract`
- `magicWand.options` (reads): Answers the current Magic Wand settings: which attributes it compares and their tolerances. No parameters.
- `paint.setFill` (writes): Sets the fill of the selection or ids (or the default fill) to a colour, a swatch, a gradient, a pattern or none; a global or spot swatch stays linked.
  - `color` string or array or object
  - `focus` boolean, default `true`, false keeps the active proxy
  - `gradient` object, {kind?: linear|radial|freeform, stops?: [{offset 0..1, color, opacity? 0..1 (or 0..100), midpoint? 0.13..0.87, swatch?: global or spot colour (or tint) swatch the stop links to (its colour comes from the swatch), tint?: 0..100}] (at least 2; default white→black), angle?: deg, start?: [x,y], end?: [x,y] (the vector in document coordinates, both or neither; type objects keep it in text space), aspect?: % (radial; without start/end the gradient is placed on each object's bounds), focal?: [x,y] (radial, with start/end: the focal point, where the first stop sits), swatch?: linked gradient swatch name}; or 0..100; or tint; its colour comes from the swatch; at least 2; default white→black; the vector in document coordinates, both or neither; type objects keep it in text space; radial; without start/end the gradient is placed on each object's bounds; radial, with start/end: the focal point, where the first stop sits
  - `ids` array
  - `item` integer or null
  - `keepModel` boolean, default `false`, in a CMYK document, RGB colours and gradient stops are stored as CMYK unless true; Gray stays Gray
  - `none` boolean, default `true`
  - `swatch` string, a global or spot colour stays linked, so swatch edits recolour it; a tint swatch links to its base at its tint; a gradient swatch is recorded as the gradient's swatch and fits each object, keeping its aspect; the built-in "[Registration]" prints on every plate
  - `tint` integer, 0 to 100; % of a global or spot `swatch`; default 100, or a tint swatch's own
- `paint.setStroke` (writes): Sets the stroke paint of the selection or ids (or the default stroke) to a colour, a swatch, a gradient, a pattern or none; use stroke.set for weight and dashes.
  - `color` string or array or object
  - `focus` boolean, default `true`, false keeps the active proxy
  - `gradient` object, {kind?: linear|radial|freeform, stops?: [{offset 0..1, color, opacity? 0..1 (or 0..100), midpoint? 0.13..0.87, swatch?: global or spot colour (or tint) swatch the stop links to (its colour comes from the swatch), tint?: 0..100}] (at least 2; default white→black), angle?: deg, start?: [x,y], end?: [x,y] (the vector in document coordinates, both or neither; type objects keep it in text space), aspect?: % (radial; without start/end the gradient is placed on each object's bounds), focal?: [x,y] (radial, with start/end: the focal point, where the first stop sits), swatch?: linked gradient swatch name}; or 0..100; or tint; its colour comes from the swatch; at least 2; default white→black; the vector in document coordinates, both or neither; type objects keep it in text space; radial; without start/end the gradient is placed on each object's bounds; radial, with start/end: the focal point, where the first stop sits
  - `ids` array
  - `item` integer or null
  - `keepModel` boolean, default `false`, in a CMYK document, RGB colours and gradient stops are stored as CMYK unless true; Gray stays Gray
  - `none` boolean, default `true`
  - `swatch` string, a global or spot colour stays linked, so swatch edits recolour it; a tint swatch links to its base at its tint; a gradient swatch is recorded as the gradient's swatch and fits each object, keeping its aspect; the built-in "[Registration]" prints on every plate
  - `tint` integer, 0 to 100; % of a global or spot `swatch`; default 100, or a tint swatch's own
- `paint.swap` (writes): Swaps the fill and stroke of the selection or ids and of the default paint.
  - `ids` array
- `paint.default` (writes): Resets the selection or ids and the default paint to a white fill and a 1 pt black stroke (type: black fill, no stroke).
  - `ids` array
- `paint.toggleActive` (reads): Brings the Fill or the Stroke proxy forward (or swaps them), which decides what paint.none and swatch clicks change; answers which is active.
  - `fill` boolean, true: bring the Fill proxy forward, false: the Stroke proxy; omitted: swap which is in front
- `paint.none` (writes): Sets whichever of fill or stroke is active to None on the selection and defaults. No parameters.
- `stroke.setAdvanced` (writes): Sets the Stroke panel's extras: arrowhead scale and swap, width-profile flip, and an art or pattern brush on the stroke.
  - `arrowScale` array, [start %, end %]
  - `brush` string or null
  - `flipProfile` string, one of `along` | `across`
  - `ids` array
  - `item` integer or null
  - `swapArrows` boolean
- `stroke.widthProfile.add` (writes): Saves the selected stroke's variable width as a named width profile in the profile list; answers its name.
  - `name` string
- `stroke.widthProfile.delete` (writes): Removes a saved width profile from the list (built-ins can't be deleted); strokes keep their widths.
  - `name` string
- `stroke.widthProfile.reset` (writes): Removes every saved width profile, keeping the built-in ones; answers how many were removed. No parameters.
- `stroke.widthProfile.list` (reads): Answers the width profiles (built-in and saved) with their width points, and which one the selected stroke uses. No parameters.
- `appearance.setItem` (writes): Edits one fill or stroke item of the targets' appearance stacks by index: its paint, opacity, blend, visibility or weight.
  - `blend` string
  - `color` string, as paint.setFill; one of several alternative parameters
  - `gradient` object
  - `ids` array, default: the selection
  - `index` integer
  - `none` boolean
  - `opacity` integer, 0 to 100
  - `swatch` string
  - `target` string, one of `object` | `contents`
  - `visible` boolean
  - `weight` number, points; strokes
- `appearance.removeItem` (writes): Removes fills or strokes by index from each target object's appearance stack.
  - `ids` array
  - `index` json[], [..] (paint-order item indices); paint-order item indices; one of several alternative parameters
  - `indices` json[], [..] (paint-order item indices); paint-order item indices; one of several alternative parameters
  - `target` string, one of `object` | `contents`
- `appearance.addEffect` (writes): Applies a live effect with its parameters to the targets or one of their appearance items (the same as effect.apply). No parameters.
- `appearance.moveItem` (writes): Moves an appearance item to another position in the targets' paint order.
  - `contents` integer
  - `from` integer or string
  - `ids` array
  - `target` string, one of `object` | `contents`
  - `to` integer
- `appearance.copyFrom` (writes): Copies the appearance of object source onto ids or the selection, as the Eyedropper does, with options for what is picked up and applied.
  - `append` boolean
  - `apply` object
  - `ids` array
  - `pickUp` object
  - `reverse` boolean
  - `source` integer, an id
- `appearance.setActiveItem` (reads): Chooses which appearance item of the first selected object later paint, stroke and effect commands target when they omit item.
  - `index` integer or null
- `appearance.targetContents` (reads): Selects the members of the selected groups and layers so later appearance edits apply to them, as double-clicking Contents does; answers the ids.
  - `ids` array
- `appearance.transfer` (writes): Gives target the appearance and transparency of source (moving it, or copying with copy), as dragging a Layers panel target circle does.
  - `copy` boolean
  - `source` integer, an id
  - `target` integer, an id
- `graphicStyle.list` (reads): Answers every graphic style with its fills, strokes, effects, transparency and the ids of objects linked to it. No parameters.
- `graphicStyle.move` (writes): Moves a graphic style to position to in the list.
  - `name` string
  - `to` integer, a position counted from 0 (the first is 0)
- `graphicStyle.setOptions` (reads): Sets whether applying a graphic style to type replaces its characters' own fill and stroke; answers the setting.
  - `overrideCharColor` boolean
- `swatch.list` (reads): Answers the document's swatches (colours, tints, gradients, patterns) with their kind, group, global/spot flags and colour values.
  - `group` string, only that colour group's swatches
- `paint.setGradientGeom` (writes): Moves the selected objects' gradient vector (start, end), radial aspect and focal point, as the Gradient tool does.
  - `aspect` number, percent; radial: the extent ellipse's height / width; default: kept
  - `end` number[], document coordinates; both or neither: omitted, the vector stays
  - `focal` array or null
  - `ids` array
  - `item` integer or null
  - `start` number[]
  - `stroke` boolean, default: the targeted item's kind, else the active proxy
- `gradient.selectStop` (reads): Selects a stop of the gradient behind the active paint proxy so later stop edits act on it; null clears it.
  - `index` integer or null
- `transparency.setOpacityMask` (writes): Changes the opacity masks of ids or the selection: clipping, inverted, disabled or linked.
  - `clip` boolean
  - `disabled` boolean
  - `invert` boolean
  - `linked` boolean
- `transparency.opacityMaskInfo` (reads): Answers the opacity masks of ids or the selection: whether each clips, is inverted, disabled or linked, and its art. No parameters.
- `transparency.info` (reads): Answers the Transparency panel values of ids or the selection: opacity, blend mode, isolation, knockout and the page's isolated-blending and knockout settings. No parameters.
- `layer.setCurrent` (reads): Highlights one Layers panel row and makes its layer the current layer where new art goes; not an undo step.
  - `id` integer or string, an id
- `layer.highlight` (reads): Highlights Layers panel rows (set, add or toggle); the last one's layer becomes current. Not an undo step.
  - `ids` array
  - `mode` string, one of `set` | `add` | `toggle`
- `layer.selectAll` (reads): Selects the visible, unlocked art of a layer (or the object itself), or adds it to the selection, as the Layers panel's selection column does.
  - `add` boolean
  - `id` integer or string, an id
- `layer.move` (writes): Moves (or copies) Layers panel rows above, below or inside a target row, as dragging in the panel does.
  - `copy` boolean
  - `ids` array
  - `place` string, one of `above` | `below` | `inside`, default inside
  - `target` integer
- `node.move` (writes): Puts a row at an index (0 = bottom) inside a parent layer or group, or at the top level.
  - `id` integer or string, an id
  - `index` integer, a position counted from 0 (the first is 0)
  - `parent` integer, an id; null = top level
- `layer.target` (reads): Targets a layer, group or object as clicking its target circle does, so appearance edits apply to it as a whole.
  - `add` boolean, Shift-click: the item joins the selection, or leaves it when all selected; nothing is targeted
  - `id` integer or string, an id
- `path.freehand` (writes): Draws a freehand path through points (with optional pen pressure), smoothed by fidelity, as the Pencil or Paintbrush does; can extend an existing path.
  - `closed` boolean
  - `extend` object
  - `fidelity` number, points; 1.5
  - `fill` boolean
  - `points` array, pen pressure 0..1: the stroke keeps it, for Calligraphic brushes with Pressure variation; a point without one presses fully
  - `style` string, one of `pencil` | `brush`
- `path.curvature` (writes): Creates a smooth path curving through the given points (or replaces path id's geometry), as the Curvature tool does; answers its id.
  - `closed` boolean
  - `id` integer or string, an id
  - `points` object[], [{x, y, corner?}]
- `path.curvatureEdit` (writes): Edits a path as the Curvature tool does: moves, inserts or extends anchors, or closes it, keeping the curve smooth elsewhere.
  - `anchor` integer
  - `end` string, one of `start` | `end`
  - `from` string, one of `keep` | `smooth` | `corner`
  - `id` integer or string, an id
  - `op` string, one of `move` | `insert` | `extend` | `close`
  - `segment` integer
  - `subpath` integer
  - `t` number
  - `x` number
  - `y` number
- `path.removeAnchor` (writes): Removes one anchor from a path and refits the curve around it.
  - `anchor` integer
  - `id` integer or string, an id
  - `subpath` integer
- `path.convertAnchor` (writes): Converts one anchor to a corner or a smooth point (optionally placing its out handle).
  - `anchor` integer
  - `id` integer or string, an id
  - `subpath` integer
  - `to` string, one of `corner` | `smooth`
  - `x` number
  - `y` number
- `path.reshapeSegment` (writes): Bends one segment so its point at parameter t moves by dx, dy.
  - `dx` number
  - `dy` number
  - `id` integer or string, an id
  - `segment` integer
  - `subpath` integer
  - `t` number
- `path.split` (writes): Splits a path at a segment parameter or an anchor: a closed path opens there, an open one becomes two; answers the ids.
  - `id` integer or string, an id
  - `segment` integer
  - `subpath` integer
  - `t` number
- `path.knife` (writes): Cuts the selected (or all) closed shapes along a freehand polyline, as the Knife does; answers the pieces' ids.
  - `points` array
- `path.eraseRegion` (writes): Erases a round-brush stroke along points from the selected (or all) paths, as the Eraser does; answers the resulting ids.
  - `points` array
  - `size` number, points; 10
- `path.eraseSegments` (writes): Erases the parts of the selected paths under a drag along points, as the Path Eraser does.
  - `points` array
  - `width` number, points; 8
- `path.smoothRegion` (writes): Smooths the selected paths near a drag along points, reducing anchors; answers before and after anchor counts.
  - `fidelity` number, points; 2.5
  - `points` array
  - `radius` number, points; 12
- `path.joinScrub` (writes): Joins the open-path endpoints a scrub along points passes over, as the Join tool does; answers the joined path's id.
  - `points` array
  - `tolerance` number, points; 12
- `path.blob` (writes): Paints a filled brush shape along points and merges it with touching blobs of the same colour, as the Blob Brush does.
  - `merge` boolean, default `true`
  - `points` array
  - `size` number, points; 10
- `object.distort` (writes): Warps the selection or ids projectively so its bounds' four corners land on the given points, as Free Distort does.
  - `corners` json[], [[x,y]×4] (TL, TR, BR, BL); TL, TR, BR, BL
  - `from` number[], [x0, y0, x1, y1]; default: selection bounds
  - `ids` array
- `paint.sampleColor` (writes): Samples a colour into the active fill or stroke (and the selection), or into one stop of the gradient behind the proxy.
  - `color` string
  - `ids` array
  - `stop` integer, a position counted from 0 (the first is 0)
  - `stroke` boolean, default: whichever proxy is active
- `eyedropper.setOptions` (reads): Sets which attributes the Eyedropper picks up and applies and its image sample size; affects appearance.copyFrom.
  - `apply` object, {appearance?: {transparency?, fill?: {color?, transparency?, overprint?}, stroke?: {color?, transparency?, overprint?, weight?, cap?, join?, miter?, dash?}}, character?, paragraph?} (bools; a bool for a branch sets all of it); bools; a bool for a branch sets all of it
  - `pickUp` object
  - `sampleSize` integer, one of `1` | `3` | `5`, pixels square averaged when sampling an image: point, 3×3, 5×5
- `artboard.move` (writes): Moves an artboard by dx, dy with the art fully inside it (or leaves it and moves copies with copy).
  - `copy` boolean
  - `dx` number
  - `dy` number
  - `index` integer, a position counted from 0 (the first is 0)
  - `moveArt` boolean
- `effect.apply` (writes): Applies a live effect (see effect.list for ids and parameters) to the selection, ids or one appearance item; the effect stays editable.
  - `effect` integer, an id; see effect.list, e.g. "stylize.dropShadow", "distort.roughen", "warp.arc", or "plugin.<id>" for an installed effect plug-in
  - `ids` json[], [..] (layers too); layers too
  - `item` integer or null
  - `params` object, missing keys take the dialog defaults
  - `target` string, one of `object` | `contents`, contents: the objects inside groups and layers
- `effect.list` (reads): Answers the catalogue of live effects with their parameters and defaults, and the effects applied to the selection. No parameters.
- `effect.remove` (writes): Removes the effect at index from the selection's (or one appearance item's) effect list.
  - `ids` json[], [..]
  - `index` integer, position in the effect list
  - `item` integer or null
- `effect.setParams` (writes): Changes the parameters or visibility of the effect at index on the selection or ids.
  - `ids` json[], [..]
  - `index` integer
  - `item` integer or null
  - `params` object, merged into the current parameters
  - `visible` boolean
- `effect.duplicate` (writes): Inserts a copy of the effect at index right after it.
  - `ids` json[], [..]
  - `index` integer
  - `item` integer or null
- `effect.move` (writes): Moves an effect within an effect list or between appearance items.
  - `copy` boolean, copy instead of move, as Alt-dragging the row
  - `from` integer, position in the source list
  - `fromItem` integer or null
  - `ids` json[], [..]
  - `to` integer, its position in the destination list afterwards
  - `toItem` integer or null
- `text.setText` (writes): Replaces the contents of type objects id or ids with text, keeping the first run's style.
  - `text` string
- `text.reshapeArea` (writes): Moves anchors of an area type frame by dx, dy so the text reflows, as dragging a frame corner does.
  - `anchors` array
  - `dx` number
  - `dy` number
  - `id` integer or string, an id
- `text.setStyle` (writes): Sets character style on type or a byte range of it: font, style, size, leading, tracking, justification, fill and OpenType features.
  - `end` integer, 0 to 255
  - `features` string[]
  - `fill` string, a colour such as #rrggbb
  - `font` string
  - `justify` string, one of `auto` | `left` | `center` | `right` | `justifyAll`, the start of each paragraph's direction
  - `leading` number or string
  - `size` number, points
  - `start` integer, 0 to 255
  - `style` string
  - `tracking` number
- `object.maskImage` (writes): Clips the selected image with a rectangle around it and selects that clipping path for cropping by its handles. No parameters.
- `object.blend.info` (reads): Answers the options of the first selected blend (spacing, steps, distance, orientation, keys, spine), else the defaults new blends get. No parameters.
- `object.blend.spine.moveAnchor` (writes): Moves a point of a blend's spine, or one of its handles, to x, y.
  - `anchor` integer, a position counted from 0 (the first is 0)
  - `handle` string, one of `in` | `out`
  - `id` integer or string, an id; default: the selected blend
  - `independent` boolean
  - `x` number
  - `y` number
- `object.blend.spine.addAnchor` (writes): Adds a point to a blend's spine where it passes nearest x, y; answers its index.
  - `id` integer or string, an id; default: the selected blend
  - `x` number
  - `y` number
- `object.blend.spine.removeAnchor` (writes): Deletes a spine point that no key object sits on.
  - `anchor` integer, a position counted from 0 (the first is 0)
  - `id` integer or string, an id; default: the selected blend
- `object.envelope.info` (reads): Answers the selected envelope's type and settings, or the defaults new envelopes get. No parameters.
- `object.envelope.setMeshPoint` (writes): Moves a point of a mesh envelope (with its handles), or one handle end, to x, y.
  - `handle` integer, one of `0` | `1` | `2` | `3`
  - `id` integer or string, an id
  - `index` integer, a position counted from 0 (the first is 0)
  - `x` number
  - `y` number
- `object.mesh.setPointColor` (writes): Sets the colour and opacity of one point of a gradient mesh.
  - `color` string
  - `id` integer or string, an id
  - `index` integer, a position counted from 0 (the first is 0)
  - `opacity` number, 0 to 1
- `object.mesh.movePoint` (writes): Moves a point of a gradient mesh or mesh envelope (with its handles), or one handle end, to x, y.
  - `handle` integer, one of `0` | `1` | `2` | `3`
  - `id` integer or string, an id
  - `index` integer, a position counted from 0 (the first is 0)
  - `x` number
  - `y` number
- `object.mesh.addLine` (writes): Adds a mesh row and column through x, y to a gradient mesh or mesh envelope; answers the new point's index.
  - `color` string
  - `id` integer or string, an id
  - `x` number
  - `y` number
- `object.mesh.deletePoint` (writes): Deletes the mesh lines through one point of a gradient mesh or mesh envelope.
  - `id` integer or string, an id
  - `index` integer, a position counted from 0 (the first is 0)
- `color.harmony` (reads): Answers a colour harmony (complementary, triad, analogous, shades and more) built from a base colour, optionally snapped to a swatch library; changes nothing.
  - `amount` integer, 0 to 100; 50; how far the outermost steps go
  - `color` string
  - `limitTo` string
  - `rule` string, one of `complementary` | `complementary2` | `splitComplementary` | `leftComplement` | `rightComplement` | `analogous` | `analogous2` | `monochromatic` | `shades` | `triad` | `triad2` | `triad3` | `tetrad` | `tetrad2` | `tetrad3` | `compound` | `compound2` | `highContrast` | `highContrast2` | `highContrast3` | `pentagram`, or its label
  - `steps` integer, 1 to 20; 4
  - `variation` string, one of `tintsShades` | `warmCool` | `vividMuted`
- `color.loadProfile` (writes): Registers an ICC colour profile from a file (native app only) so it can be used as a working space; answers its name and kind.
  - `path` file, .icc/.icm file
- `color.convert` (reads): Converts a colour to RGB, CMYK, grey or Lab through the working spaces and answers its values, hex and whether it is out of gamut.
  - `color` string
  - `intent` string, one of `perceptual` | `relative` | `saturation` | `absolute`
  - `to` string, one of `rgb` | `cmyk` | `gray` | `lab`
- `color.gamutCheck` (reads): Answers the colours of the selection (or document) that can't print in the working CMYK, with how far out and how often used.
  - `colors` string[]
  - `ids` array
- `view.separationsPreview` (reads): Shows chosen ink plates in Separations Preview (one plate as greyscale coverage); answers the plates.
  - `on` boolean
  - `only` string
  - `plates` json[], [names]
  - `toggle` string
- `color.plates` (reads): Answers the document's ink plates (process and spot) and which are visible in Separations Preview. No parameters.
- `swatch.setSpot` (writes): Makes a swatch a spot colour (or a process colour again); spot swatches print on their own plate.
  - `name` string
  - `spot` boolean, default `true`
- `text.editRange` (writes): Replaces bytes start..end of a type object's plain text with insert or styled runs; answers the caret position.
  - `end` integer, 0 to 255
  - `id` integer or string, an id
  - `insert` string
  - `runs` object[]
  - `start` integer, 0 to 255
- `text.setRangeStyle` (writes): Sets character attributes on a byte range of one type object (default all its text): font, size, leading, tracking, kerning, scale, rotation, fill, stroke and more.
  - `allCaps` boolean
  - `baselineShift` number, points
  - `charAlign` string, one of `romanBaseline` | `emBoxTop` | `emBoxCenter` | `emBoxBottom` | `icfTop` | `icfBottom`
  - `end` integer, 0 to 255; default: all text
  - `features` string[]
  - `fill` string, a colour such as #rrggbb
  - `font` string
  - `hScale` number, percent
  - `id` integer or string, an id; default: the one selected type object
  - `kerning` number or string
  - `leading` number or string
  - `position` string, one of `normal` | `superscript` | `subscript`, sizes from Document Setup
  - `rotation` number, degrees
  - `size` number, points
  - `smallCaps` boolean
  - `start` integer, 0 to 255
  - `strikethrough` boolean
  - `stroke` string, a colour such as #rrggbb
  - `strokeOptions` object, {weight?, cap?, join?, miterLimit?, dash?, dashOffset?, alignDashes?} (as stroke.set: the character stroke); as stroke.set: the character stroke
  - `strokeWidth` number, points
  - `style` string
  - `tracking` number
  - `underline` boolean
  - `vScale` number, percent
- `text.getRange` (reads): Answers a type object's text (or a byte range of it) with its styled runs and length; the document is unchanged.
  - `end` number
  - `id` integer or string, an id
  - `start` number
- `text.createInPath` (writes): Puts new type inside a closed path (area type) or along a path (type on a path) with text, font and fit options; answers its id.
  - `at` number[], on-path start: nearest point
  - `charAlign` string
  - `color` string, as text.create
  - `fit` string, one of `none` | `autoHeight` | `shrinkText`
  - `fitMinPercent` number
  - `font` string
  - `leadingModel` string, one of `romanBaseline` | `emBoxTop`
  - `mode` string, one of `area` | `onPath`
  - `path` integer, an id
  - `placeholder` boolean, placeholder text instead, as text.create
  - `size` number
  - `style` string
  - `text` string, like
  - `vertical` boolean, default `false`
- `type.step` (writes): Steps a type attribute (size, leading, tracking, kerning, baseline shift) up or down by the preference increments.
  - `attribute` string, one of `size` | `leading` | `tracking` | `kerning` | `baselineShift`
  - `by` integer
  - `end` integer, 0 to 255
  - `id` integer or string, an id
  - `start` integer, 0 to 255
- `type.size.increase` (writes): Increases the selected text's font size by a number of preference steps.
  - `by` integer
- `type.size.decrease` (writes): Decreases the selected text's font size by a number of preference steps.
  - `by` integer
- `text.discardEmpty` (writes): Removes type object id when it has no characters, dropping the steps that created it when nothing else changed.
  - `id` integer or string, an id
- `charStyle.list` (reads): Answers the document's character styles with their attributes and how many runs use each. No parameters.
- `charStyle.apply` (writes): Applies a character style to the selection, ids or a byte range, optionally clearing overrides; answers how many runs changed.
  - `clearOverrides` boolean
  - `name` string
- `charStyle.setAttrs` (writes): Replaces a character style's attributes; text using it updates and keeps its overrides.
  - `attrs` object
  - `name` string
- `charStyle.rename` (writes): Renames a character style.
  - `name` string
  - `to` string
- `paraStyle.list` (reads): Answers the document's paragraph styles with their attributes and how many paragraphs use each. No parameters.
- `paraStyle.apply` (writes): Applies a paragraph style to the paragraphs of the selection, ids or a byte range, optionally clearing overrides.
  - `clearOverrides` boolean
  - `name` string
- `paraStyle.setAttrs` (writes): Replaces a paragraph style's attributes; paragraphs using it update and keep their overrides.
  - `attrs` object
  - `name` string
- `paraStyle.rename` (writes): Renames a paragraph style.
  - `name` string
  - `to` string
- `text.fonts` (reads): Answers the fonts the document's type uses, with how they resolve (exact, substitute, missing) and missing glyphs.
  - `selectionOnly` boolean
- `text.replaceFont` (writes): Replaces one font (family and optionally style) with another in all text or only the selection; answers runs changed.
  - `from` object
  - `selectionOnly` boolean
  - `to` object, any of its names; stored as the font's own family name
- `select.font` (reads): Selects the type objects that use a font family (and style); answers the count.
  - `family` string
  - `style` string
- `text.fontList` (reads): Answers the font families available to the kit (bundled, added and installed), by their canonical names for text.setStyle.
  - `family` string
- `text.rescanFonts` (writes): Rescans the system font folders for fonts installed or removed since start; text in newly available fonts redraws. No parameters.
- `text.missingFonts` (reads): Answers the fonts the document's type and symbols use that aren't available as named, with what they resolve to. No parameters.
- `text.findFontFiles` (reads): Searches a folder for font files matching the document's missing fonts (or given ones) and answers what it found.
  - `folder` file, an absolute path
  - `fonts` object[], 1 to 1000; default: the active document's missing fonts, as text.missingFonts lists them
  - `maxSeconds` integer, default `60`, 1 to 600
  - `stop` boolean, default `false`, true: stop the last search
- `text.addFontFiles` (reads): Copies font files found by text.findFontFiles into the kit's own Fonts folder so they become available.
  - `files` file[], [paths the last text.findFontFiles search found] (1 to 1000); 1 to 1000
- `text.thread.info` (reads): Answers every text thread in the document as ordered lists of frame ids. No parameters.
- `graph.create` (writes): Creates a graph (column, bar, line, area, scatter, pie, radar) in a box from series, categories and rows or CSV; answers its id.
  - `categories` json[], [..]
  - `csv` string
  - `height` number
  - `rows` array[], [[number|null]]
  - `series` json[], [..]
  - `type` string, one of `column` | `stackedColumn` | `bar` | `stackedBar` | `line` | `area` | `scatter` | `pie` | `radar`
  - `width` number
  - `x` number
  - `y` number
- `view.saved.list` (reads): Answers the document's saved views with their centre, zoom and rotation. No parameters.
- `text.tabs.get` (reads): Answers the tab stops of the first selected text object's paragraph.
  - `ids` array
  - `start` integer, 0 to 255
- `select.savedList` (reads): Answers the names of the active document's saved selections. No parameters.
- `guide.add` (writes): Adds a vertical or horizontal ruler guide at a position, across the canvas or one artboard, on a layer.
  - `artboard` integer, a position counted from 0 (the first is 0); an artboard guide: it runs across that artboard only and moves, is copied and is deleted with it; default a canvas guide, across the whole canvas
  - `layer` integer, an id; the layer it is on, shown, hidden, locked and deleted with it; default the current layer
  - `pos` number, points; x for vertical, y for horizontal
  - `vertical` boolean
- `guide.list` (reads): Answers the ruler guides with their orientation, position, selection, artboard and layer. No parameters.
- `guide.select` (writes): Selects ruler guides by index on their own (or toggles them), deselecting art.
  - `indexes` array
  - `toggle` boolean
- `guide.remove` (writes): Deletes ruler guide index, else the selected guides; answers how many.
  - `index` integer, a position counted from 0 (the first is 0)
- `guide.move` (writes): Moves ruler guide index to a position, or the selected guides by dx/dy, optionally as copies.
  - `index` integer, a position counted from 0 (the first is 0)
  - `pos` number, points
- `guide.setLayer` (writes): Moves ruler guides (by index or the selected ones) to a layer; answers how many.
  - `index` integer, a position counted from 0 (the first is 0)
  - `indexes` array
  - `layer` integer, an id
- `variable.list` (reads): Answers the document's variables with their kinds and how many objects each is bound to. No parameters.
- `variable.highlight` (writes): Highlights one row in the Variables panel, which its Delete and Options act on; not an undo step.
  - `variable` string
- `dataset.list` (reads): Answers the datasets with their values, the active one, and which the art still matches. No parameters.
- `artboard.reorder` (writes): Changes an artboard's number in the artboard order.
  - `index` integer, a position counted from 0 (the first is 0)
  - `to` integer
- `artboard.copy` (writes): Copies an artboard (and optionally its art) to the clipboard so a paste adds it again here or in another document.
  - `art` boolean
  - `index` integer, a position counted from 0 (the first is 0)
- `artboard.cut` (writes): Copies an artboard (and optionally its art) to the clipboard, then deletes it and that art in one undo step.
  - `art` boolean
  - `index` integer, a position counted from 0 (the first is 0)
- `text.setFormat` (writes): Sets character and paragraph formats on type: kerning, baseline shift, scaling, rotation, underline, caps, position, indents, spacing and alignment.
  - `allCaps` boolean
  - `baselineShift` number, points
  - `burasagari` string, one of `none` | `standard` | `forced`, Paragraph panel menu › Burasagari None/Regular/Force: an East Asian comma or full stop ending an area type line hangs outside it: when it doesn't fit, or always; new type: "standard"
  - `charAlign` string, one of `romanBaseline` | `emBoxTop` | `emBoxCenter` | `emBoxBottom` | `icfTop` | `icfBottom`, where characters smaller than the largest on their line line up with it
  - `composer` string, one of `singleLine` | `everyLine`, line breaking, Every-line by default
  - `direction` string, one of `auto` | `leftToRight` | `rightToLeft`, paragraph direction; auto: from each paragraph's first strong character
  - `end` integer, 0 to 255
  - `firstLineIndent` number
  - `hScale` number, percent
  - `hyphenate` boolean
  - `kerning` number or string
  - `kinsoku` string, one of `none` | `hard` | `soft`, Kinsoku Set: Soft lets 々, ー and small kana start a line
  - `leadingModel` string, one of `romanBaseline` | `emBoxTop`, leading measured baseline to baseline, or em box top to top
  - `leftIndent` number
  - `mojikumi` string, one of `none` | `lineEndHalf`, Japanese punctuation spacing
  - `position` string, one of `normal` | `superscript` | `subscript`, sizes from Document Setup
  - `rightIndent` number
  - `rotation` number, degrees
  - `smallCaps` boolean
  - `spaceAfter` number, points; ±1296
  - `spaceBefore` number
  - `start` integer, 0 to 255
  - `strikethrough` boolean
  - `underline` boolean
  - `vScale` number, percent
- `shapeBuilder.merge` (writes): Merges (or erases) the regions a drag along points passes through, as the Shape Builder does; see shapeBuilder.regions for the regions.
  - `erase` boolean, erase mode, Alt: deletes the regions touched, and the pieces of unfilled open paths and the edges (outline pieces between the points where paths meet; see shapeBuilder.regions) within tolerance; a deleted edge opens its path there, and edges bounding a deleted region go with it
  - `fill` string or object
  - `ids` array, default: selection
  - `points` array, drag path; one point = click
  - `tolerance` number, points; 2, erase only
- `shapeBuilder.regions` (reads): Answers the faces, line pieces and edges the Shape Builder sees among the selected or given paths, with their bounds and sources.
  - `ids` array
- `livePaint.fill` (writes): Fills the Region Paint face containing a point with a colour, swatch, gradient or none.
  - `color` string, default: current fill; one of several alternative parameters
  - `gradient` object
  - `group` integer
  - `none` boolean
  - `point` number[]
  - `swatch` string
- `livePaint.strokeEdge` (writes): Paints the Region Paint edge nearest a point with a stroke colour, swatch or none and a width.
  - `color` string, default: current stroke; one of several alternative parameters
  - `group` integer, an id
  - `none` boolean
  - `point` number[]
  - `swatch` string
  - `tolerance` number, points; 4
  - `width` number, points; default: current weight
- `livePaint.info` (reads): Answers a Region Paint group's faces with their fills and edges with their strokes.
  - `group` integer
- `imageTrace.setView` (writes): Sets how Image Trace objects draw on screen (result, outlines, source image); exports keep the tracing result.
  - `id` integer
  - `ids` integer[]
  - `view` string, one of `tracingResult` | `tracingResultWithOutlines` | `outlines` | `outlinesWithSourceImage` | `sourceImage`
- `imageTrace.presets` (reads): Answers the Image Trace presets with their parameters. No parameters.
- `shaper.scribble` (writes): Applies a Shaper tool scribble along points: removes fills, merges regions or erases stroke pieces of nearby art.
  - `ids` array, default: nearby art
  - `points` array
  - `tolerance` number, points; 4
- `shaper.select` (writes): Selects a Shaper group then a face at a point, or enters construction isolation to select an original path.
  - `point` number[]
  - `source` boolean
- `brush.list` (reads): Answers the document's brushes with their types and the current brush. No parameters.
- `brush.get` (reads): Answers one brush's full definition as JSON.
  - `name` string
- `brush.apply` (writes): Applies a brush to the strokes of the selected or given paths (adding a stroke if missing) and makes it current.
  - `ids` array
  - `name` string
- `brush.remove` (writes): Removes brushes from the selected strokes, leaving plain strokes.
  - `ids` array
- `brush.setCurrent` (writes): Sets the brush the Paintbrush paints with; not an undo step.
  - `name` string or null
- `brush.new` (writes): Creates a calligraphic, scatter, art, pattern or bristle brush, from parameters or the selected art; answers its name.
  - `ids` array
  - `name` string
  - `params` object
  - `type` string, one of `calligraphic` | `scatter` | `art` | `pattern` | `bristle`
- `brush.delete` (writes): Deletes a brush; strokes using it become plain strokes.
  - `name` string
- `brush.duplicate` (writes): Duplicates a brush under a new name and answers it.
  - `name` string
  - `newName` string
- `brush.options` (writes): Changes a brush's definition fields (see brush.get); out-of-range values are clamped.
  - `name` string
  - `newName` string
  - `params` object, {…fields to change (brush.get shows them; values outside their ranges are clamped). calligraphic: angle −180..180°, roundness 0..100%, size 0..1296 pt, variation: [angle°, roundness%, size pt], modes: [fixed|random|pressure for angle, roundness, size] (pressure goes from value − variation at the lightest pen pressure to value + variation at the heaviest). scatter: size [a, b] 1..10000%, spacing [a, b] 1..10000%, scatter [a, b] −1000..1000%, rotation [a, b] −180..180°, modes: [fixed|random|pressure for size, spacing, scatter, rotation] (fixed: a; random: between a and b; pressure: a at the lightest pen pressure to b at the heaviest), rotation_relative_to_path. art: width 1..1000%, scale: {mode: proportional|stretch|betweenGuides, start, end: 0..1 of the art length}, direction: leftToRight|rightToLeft|topToBottom|bottomToTop, flip_along, flip_across. pattern: scale 1..10000%, spacing 0..10000%, fit: stretch|addSpace|approximate, flip_along, flip_across. scatter, art and pattern: colorization: {method: none|tints|tintsAndShades|hueShift, key: colour (hueShift: the art colour that becomes the stroke colour)}}; brush.get shows them; values outside their ranges are clamped; pressure goes from value − variation at the lightest pen pressure to value + variation at the heaviest; fixed: a; random: between a and b; pressure: a at the lightest pen pressure to b at the heaviest; hueShift: the art colour that becomes the stroke colour
- `object.expandBrush` (writes): Replaces brushed paths in the selection with groups of their brush art.
  - `ids` array
- `brush.freehand` (writes): Paints a freehand stroke along points with a brush, as the Paintbrush does; answers its id.
  - `brush` string
- `symbol.list` (reads): Answers the document's symbols with their instance counts and sizes, and the current symbol. No parameters.
- `symbol.new` (writes): Makes a symbol from the selection and replaces the selection with an instance; answers both.
  - `ids` array
  - `name` string
- `symbol.place` (writes): Places an instance of a symbol (default the current one) centred at x, y; answers its id.
  - `name` string
  - `x` number
  - `y` number
- `symbol.breakLink` (writes): Expands the selected symbol instances into plain art.
  - `ids` array
- `symbol.edit` (writes): Breaks the link of the selected instance so its art can be edited; finish with symbol.update.
  - `id` integer or string, an id
- `symbol.update` (writes): Redefines a symbol with the selected art; all its instances update.
  - `ids` array
  - `name` string
- `symbol.delete` (writes): Deletes a symbol, expanding its instances (or deleting them).
  - `expandInstances` boolean, default `true`
  - `name` string
- `symbol.duplicate` (writes): Duplicates a symbol under a new name and answers it.
  - `name` string
  - `newName` string
- `symbol.replace` (writes): Swaps the symbol of the selected instances for another.
  - `ids` array
  - `name` string
- `symbol.setCurrent` (writes): Sets the symbol the symbolism tools spray; not an undo step.
  - `name` string
- `symbol.selectInstances` (reads): Selects every instance of a symbol; answers the count.
  - `name` string
- `symbol.spray` (writes): Sprays symbol instances along points into a symbol set (or removes them with alt), as the Symbol Sprayer does.
  - `alt` boolean, remove instances
  - `density` integer, 1 to 10; 5
  - `name` string
  - `points` array
  - `radius` integer, default `40`
  - `scale` integer, default `1`
- `symbol.adjust` (writes): Adjusts symbol instances near points with a symbolism tool: shift, scrunch, size, spin, stain, screen or style.
  - `alt` boolean
  - `color` string
  - `intensity` integer, 1 to 10; 5
  - `points` array
  - `radius` integer, default `40`
  - `style` string
  - `tool` string, one of `shift` | `scrunch` | `size` | `spin` | `stain` | `screen` | `style`
- `object.pattern.done` (writes): Leaves pattern editing mode, saving the tile art into the pattern. No parameters.
- `object.pattern.cancel` (writes): Leaves pattern editing mode, discarding the tile changes. No parameters.
- `object.pattern.saveCopy` (writes): While editing a pattern, saves the current tile as a new pattern swatch; answers its name.
  - `name` string
- `pattern.delete` (writes): Deletes a pattern swatch; objects painted with it lose that paint.
  - `name` string
- `pattern.list` (reads): Answers the document's patterns with their tile types and sizes, and which is being edited. No parameters.
- `pattern.transform` (writes): Transforms only the placement of the selected objects' pattern paints by a matrix, leaving the objects.
  - `ids` array
  - `matrix` number[], [a, b, c, d, e, f]
- `object.repeat.expand` (writes): Replaces the selected repeats with groups of their instances. No parameters.
- `prefs.get` (reads): Answers one preference's value (or group), or all preferences.
  - `key` string
- `prefs.set` (reads): Sets one or more preferences after validating them (see prefs.list for keys and kinds).
  - `key` string
  - `value` json
- `prefs.reset` (reads): Resets one preference category, or all preferences, to their defaults.
  - `category` string
- `prefs.list` (reads): Answers every preference with its key, category, label, kind and current value. No parameters.
- `stroke.widthPoint.set` (writes): Adds or moves a width point on a path's stroke at fraction t with left and right widths, as the Width tool does.
  - `adjustAdjoining` boolean, with index: the nearest points either side change their widths in proportion
  - `id` integer or string, an id
  - `index` integer
  - `left` number
  - `right` number
  - `t` number, 0 to 1; fraction of the path length
- `stroke.widthPoint.remove` (writes): Removes width points from a path's stroke; removing the last one leaves a uniform stroke.
  - `id` integer or string, an id
  - `index` json[], [..]; one of several alternative parameters
  - `indices` json[], [..]; one of several alternative parameters
- `stroke.widthPoint.copy` (writes): Copies a width point to another position along the stroke.
  - `id` integer or string, an id
  - `index` integer
  - `t` number, 0 to 1
- `stroke.widthProfile.set` (writes): Sets a variable width profile on strokes as [t, left, right] factors, or null for a uniform stroke.
  - `points` array or null
- `object.liquify` (writes): Applies a Liquify tool (warp, twirl, pucker, bloat, scallop, crystallize, wrinkle) along a brush stroke of points to the selected art.
  - `affectAnchors` boolean
  - `affectIn` boolean
  - `affectOut` boolean
  - `angle` number
  - `complexity` integer
  - `detail` integer
  - `height` number, pt, default 100
  - `horizontal` number
  - `ids` array, default: selection, else every path the brush touches
  - `intensity` number
  - `points` array, the brush stroke; pen pressure 0..1, default 1
  - `rate` number
  - `simplify` number
  - `tool` string, one of `warp` | `twirl` | `pucker` | `bloat` | `scallop` | `crystallize` | `wrinkle`
  - `usePressure` boolean, each point's pressure is the intensity there
  - `vertical` number
- `object.pinWarp` (writes): Warps the selected art by moving warp pins from their positions to targets (optionally turning around pins).
  - `angles` array, same length: the turn the art takes around each pin, as Alt-dragging around a pin does; null leaves it free
  - `expand` number, points
  - `id` integer or string, an id; default: selection; one of several alternative parameters
  - `ids` array, default: selection; one of several alternative parameters
  - `moved` array, targets, same length
  - `pins` array, current pin positions
  - `rest` boolean
- `object.pinWarp.pins` (writes): Answers (and sets up) the warp pins on the selected art: where each started, where it is now and the turn it holds.
  - `expand` number, points
  - `id` integer or string, an id; default: selection; one of several alternative parameters
  - `ids` array, default: selection; one of several alternative parameters
- `perspective.grid.set` (writes): Merges settings into the document's perspective grid: kind, origin, horizon, vanishing points, distance, cell size, extent and plane offsets.
  - `cell` number
  - `distance` number
  - `extent` number
  - `groundOffset` number, points; planes moved along their normals
  - `height` number
  - `horizon` number
  - `kind` integer, one of `1` | `2` | `3`
  - `leftOffset` number
  - `origin` number[]
  - `plane` string, one of `left` | `right` | `ground` | `none`
  - `reproject` boolean
  - `rightOffset` number
  - `visible` boolean
  - `vpLeft` number[]
  - `vpRight` number[]
  - `vpVertical` number[]
- `perspective.grid.preset` (writes): Resets the perspective grid to a 1-, 2- or 3-point preset fitted to the first artboard and shows it.
  - `kind` integer, one of `1` | `2` | `3`
- `perspective.grid.show` (writes): Shows, hides or toggles the perspective grid; view state, not an undo step.
  - `visible` boolean
- `perspective.plane.set` (writes): Sets the active perspective plane (left, right, ground or none) that drawing and attaching use; not an undo step.
  - `plane` string, one of `left` | `right` | `ground` | `none`
- `perspective.attach` (writes): Projects the selected or given objects onto a perspective plane (default the active one).
  - `ids` array
  - `plane` string, one of `left` | `right` | `ground`, default: the active plane
- `perspective.release` (writes): Detaches objects from the perspective grid without changing their geometry.
  - `ids` array
- `perspective.move` (writes): Slides objects within their perspective plane (or along its normal) from one point to another, optionally as copies.
  - `copy` boolean, move copies, as Alt-dragging does
  - `from` number[]
  - `ids` array
  - `perpendicular` boolean, move along the plane's normal instead, as pressing 5 while dragging does
  - `plane` string, one of `left` | `right` | `ground`
  - `snap` boolean, default: View › Perspective Grid › Snap to Grid
  - `to` number[]
- `perspective.draw` (writes): Runs a shape command and attaches the result to a perspective plane, snapping its corners to the gridlines.
  - `command` string
  - `params` object
  - `plane` string, one of `left` | `right` | `ground`
  - `snap` boolean, default: Snap to Grid
- `perspective.transform` (writes): Transforms objects within their own perspective planes by a matrix in plane coordinates, with optional depth and copy.
  - `copy` boolean
  - `depth` number
  - `ids` array
  - `matrix` number[], [a, b, c, d, e, f]; affine map in plane coordinates, points: u along the plane, v up or away
  - `plane` string, one of `left` | `right` | `ground`
- `perspective.nudge` (writes): Nudges the selection in perspective by the keyboard increment, as the arrow keys do with the Perspective Selection tool.
  - `big` boolean, ×10
  - `copy` boolean
  - `dx` number
  - `dy` integer, one of `-1` | `0` | `1`
- `perspective.plane.move` (writes): Moves a perspective plane along its normal, optionally moving or copying the objects on it.
  - `objects` string, one of `none` | `move` | `copy`, default none: the objects on the plane stay; move: they move with it, as Shift-dragging a plane widget does; copy: copies of them do, as Alt-dragging does
  - `offset` number
  - `plane` string, one of `left` | `right` | `ground`, default: the active plane
- `perspective.plane.matchObject` (writes): Moves the plane an object is attached to onto the object and makes it the active plane.
  - `id` integer or string, an id; default: the first selected object
- `perspective.editText` (writes): Shows type in perspective flat in isolation mode for editing; exiting isolation projects it again.
  - `id` integer or string, an id; default: the selected type
- `paint.invert` (writes): Inverts the active proxy's (fill's or stroke's) colours of the selection, keeping each colour's model.
  - `ids` array
  - `stroke` boolean, default: the active proxy
- `paint.complement` (writes): Replaces the active proxy's colours of the selection with their complements, keeping each colour's model.
  - `ids` array
  - `stroke` boolean, default: the active proxy
- `paint.lastColor` (writes): Applies the last solid colour used to the active proxy of the selection and defaults.
  - `ids` array
  - `stroke` boolean, default: the active proxy
- `paint.lastGradient` (writes): Applies the last gradient used, fitted to each object, to the active proxy of the selection and defaults.
  - `ids` array
  - `stroke` boolean, default: the active proxy
- `paint.recent` (reads): Answers the recently used colours (newest first) and the last colour and gradient. No parameters.
- `paint.proxies` (reads): Answers the paints the Fill and Stroke proxies show (from the selection or the defaults for new art) and which is active. No parameters.
- `object.setOverprint` (writes): Makes fills and/or strokes of the selection or one appearance item overprint, or knock out.
  - `fill` boolean
  - `ids` array
  - `item` integer or null
  - `stroke` boolean
- `attributes.info` (reads): Answers the Attributes panel values of the selection: overprint, centre point, image map, URL, note, fill rule and path direction.
  - `ids` array
  - `item` integer
- `swatch.library.list` (reads): Answers every swatch library (built-in, user and loaded) with its category and swatch count. No parameters.
- `swatch.library.get` (reads): Answers one swatch library's swatches and colour groups.
  - `library` string
- `paint.freeform.addPoint` (writes): Adds a colour point to the freeform gradient on the selection's fill or stroke at a position, with colour, opacity and spread.
  - `at` number[], document coordinates
  - `color` string, default: the gradient's colour there
  - `ids` array
  - `item` integer or null
  - `line` boolean, default `true`, join it to the selected point: extends the line ending there, else starts one
  - `stroke` boolean, default: the targeted item's kind, else the active proxy
- `paint.freeform.setPoint` (writes): Edits a freeform gradient point: position, colour, opacity or spread.
  - `at` number[], document coordinates
  - `color` string
  - `ids` array
  - `index` integer, a position counted from 0 (the first is 0); default: the selected point
  - `item` integer or null
  - `stroke` boolean, default: the targeted item's kind, else the active proxy
- `paint.freeform.deletePoint` (writes): Removes a point from a freeform gradient (never the last one).
  - `ids` array
  - `index` integer, a position counted from 0 (the first is 0); default: the selected point
