  - `item` integer or null
  - `stroke` boolean, default: the targeted item's kind, else the active proxy
- `paint.freeform.addLine` (writes): Joins freeform gradient points with a smooth line along which colour blends.
  - `ids` array
  - `item` integer or null
  - `points` integer[], at least two
  - `stroke` boolean, default: the targeted item's kind, else the active proxy
- `paint.freeform.splitLine` (writes): Splits a freeform gradient line by adding a point on one of its segments.
  - `ids` array
  - `item` integer or null
  - `line` integer
  - `segment` integer
  - `stroke` boolean, default: the targeted item's kind, else the active proxy
  - `t` number, 0 to 1; default 0.5
- `paint.freeform.selectPoint` (writes): Selects a freeform gradient point so the Gradient tool and panels act on it; null clears it.
  - `index` integer or null
- `paint.freeform.get` (reads): Answers the freeform gradient behind the first selected object's fill or stroke: its mode, points, lines and selected point.
  - `stroke` boolean, default: the active proxy
- `flattener.presets.list` (reads): Answers the transparency flattener presets, built-in and saved, with their options. No parameters.
- `flattener.presets.save` (reads): Creates or changes a saved transparency flattener preset from options; answers it.
  - `name` string, default: a new "Flattener Preset N"
  - `newName` string
  - `preset` string
- `flattener.presets.delete` (reads): Deletes a saved transparency flattener preset (built-in ones stay).
  - `name` string
- `flattener.presets.import` (reads): Imports transparency flattener presets from a .vcflattener file.
  - `replace` boolean, default `false`, replace saved presets of the same names; else the imported ones get a number
- `flattener.presets.export` (reads): Writes transparency flattener presets as a .vcflattener file, or answers its text.
  - `names` array, [preset names, built-in ones too] (default: every saved preset); default: every saved preset
  - `path` file
- `flattener.preview` (reads): Answers which areas flattening would rasterize, outline or expand, as the Flattener Preview panel highlights them.
  - `highlight` string, one of `none` | `rasterizedRegions` | `transparentObjects` | `allAffected` | `expandedPatterns` | `outlinedStrokes` | `outlinedText` | `allRasterized`, areas the raster/vector balance rasterizes whole; pattern art taking part; default none
  - `ids` array, default: the whole document
  - `overprints` string, one of `preserve` | `simulate` | `discard`, simulate and discard flatten without preserveOverprints
  - `preset` string
- `graphicStyle.libraries` (reads): Answers every graphic style library (built-in, user and loaded) with its style count. No parameters.
- `graphicStyle.library` (reads): Answers one graphic style library's styles.
  - `library` string
- `library.list` (reads): Answers the shared libraries with counts of their graphics, colours and styles, and the current library. No parameters.
- `library.get` (reads): Answers one library's graphics (with thumbnails), colours, character and paragraph styles and groups.
  - `library` string
- `library.setCurrent` (writes): Sets which library the Libraries panel shows and library commands without a library act on.
  - `library` string
- `library.create` (writes): Creates a new empty library and makes it current; answers its id and name.
  - `name` string, like My Library
- `library.rename` (writes): Renames a library (default the current one).
  - `library` string
  - `name` string
- `library.delete` (writes): Deletes a library and its file; not undoable.
  - `library` string
- `library.add` (writes): Adds an item from the selection to a library: a graphic, a fill or stroke colour, or a character or paragraph style.
  - `ids` integer[]
  - `kind` string, one of `graphic` | `fillColor` | `strokeColor` | `charStyle` | `paraStyle`
  - `library` string
  - `name` string
- `library.use` (writes): Uses a library item: places a graphic copy, or applies a colour or style to the selection.
  - `center` number[], graphic; default: the first artboard's centre
  - `item` string, graphic: id or name
  - `kind` string, one of `graphic` | `fillColor` | `strokeColor` | `charStyle` | `paraStyle`
  - `library` string
  - `to` string, one of `fill` | `stroke`, colours; default: the kind's
- `library.removeItem` (writes): Deletes an item from a library.
  - `item` string, graphic: id or name
  - `kind` string, one of `graphic` | `fillColor` | `strokeColor` | `charStyle` | `paraStyle`
  - `library` string
- `library.createGroup` (writes): Creates a group of library items, moving the given items into it.
  - `items` object[], [{kind, item}] (moved into it out of their groups); moved into it out of their groups
  - `library` string
  - `name` string, like Group; a name the library's groups have, ignoring case, gets a number
- `library.renameGroup` (writes): Renames a group in a library.
  - `group` string
  - `library` string
  - `name` string
- `library.deleteGroup` (writes): Deletes a library group; its items stay in the library ungrouped.
  - `group` string
  - `library` string
- `library.moveItem` (writes): Moves a library item into a group, or out of its group.
  - `group` string, null or none: out of its group
  - `item` string, graphic: id or name
  - `kind` string, one of `graphic` | `fillColor` | `strokeColor` | `charStyle` | `paraStyle`
  - `library` string
- `library.export` (reads): Writes a library as a .vclibrary file, or answers its text.
  - `library` string
  - `path` file
- `library.import` (reads): Adds the library of a .vclibrary file as a new current library.
  - `name` string
- `object.expand.info` (reads): Answers what each Expand option (object, fill, stroke) would change in the selection. No parameters.
- `attributes.set` (writes): Sets Attributes panel values on the selection: overprint fill and stroke, centre point display, image map, URL and note.
  - `ids` array
  - `imageMap` string, one of `none` | `rectangle` | `polygon`
  - `note` string
  - `overprintFill` boolean
  - `overprintStroke` boolean, aimed as object.setOverprint's fill and stroke, item? too
  - `showCenter` boolean, the canvas shows the selected object's centre point
  - `url` string, "" removes it; SVG export links the object
- `path.setFillRule` (writes): Sets the fill rule (non-zero or even-odd) of the selected or given paths and compound paths.
  - `ids` array
  - `rule` string, one of `nonZero` | `evenOdd`
- `appearance.newArt` (reads): Answers the appearance, opacity, blend and graphic style the next object drawn will get. No parameters.
- `colorTheme.list` (reads): Answers the saved colour themes with their colours and harmony rules. No parameters.
- `document.exportPdf` (writes): Writes the document's artboards as a PDF with a preset or options (standard, compression, marks, bleed, layers, security), or answers the data.
  - `advanced` object, below 100 is accepted with a warning: fonts are always embedded as subsets; type as real, selectable and searchable text in embedded subset fonts with a ToUnicode map; fonts whose licence forbids embedding, or allows only whole fonts, stay outlines with a warning; true: every glyph as an outline; overprinting fills and strokes set /OP /op true, /OPM 1; white ones knock out with document.setup discardWhiteOverprint; they knock out
  - `bleed` number or array or object
  - `compatibility` number, default `1.3`, no transparency: it is flattened with flattenerPreset; images keep no see-through pixels; default; choosing a standard sets its version: 1.7 for pdfA2b, 1.6 for pdfX4, 1.3 for pdfX1a and pdfX3, which write 1.4 as 1.3 too; pdfA2b refuses 1.3
  - `compression` object, {color?, gray?: {downsample: none|average|subsample|bicubic, ppi: 300, abovePpi: 450, compression: none|zip|jpeg|jpeg2000|auto, quality: minimum|low|medium|high|maximum}, mono?: {downsample, ppi: 1200, abovePpi: 1800, compression: none|ccittG3|ccittG4|zip|runLength} (black-and-white images), compressText?: true} (images above abovePpi are resampled to ppi; auto keeps JPEGs JPEG, the others lossless; JPEG needs opaque images; none, jpeg2000, CCITT and runLength are written as ZIP with a warning); black-and-white images; images above abovePpi are resampled to ppi; auto keeps JPEGs JPEG, the others lossless; JPEG needs opaque images; none, jpeg2000, CCITT and runLength are written as ZIP with a warning
  - `createLayers` boolean
  - `fastWebView` boolean
  - `flattener` object
  - `flattenerPreset` string
  - `includeNonPrinting` boolean, keep layers whose Print option is off; left out by default unless createLayers
  - `marks` object, {trim, registration, colorBars, pageInfo, kind: roman|japanese, weight: 0.25 (trim marks and targets), offset: 6 (pt from the artboard, at least the bleed)} (printer's marks in [Registration], every plate: trim marks, registration targets mid-side, CMYK/spot/black-tint colour bars on top, page information (title, artboard, date UTC) below); trim marks and targets; pt from the artboard, at least the bleed; printer's marks in [Registration], every plate: trim marks, registration targets mid-side, CMYK/spot/black-tint colour bars on top, page information (title, artboard, date UTC) below
  - `output` object, {conversion: none (default)|destination (every colour into the destination profile's model, CMYK or RGB, also colours of that model in another profile)|preserveNumbers (only colours of the other model and Lab; those in the destination's model keep their numbers) (grey stays grey; images are converted too, printer's marks are not), destination: profile name (edit.colorSettings lists them; default: the document's profile for its colour mode), profiles: none (device colours)|all|destination|taggedSource (documents assigned a profile: edit.assignProfile) (ICC-based colours: CMYK with the destination or document CMYK profile, RGB as sRGB, grey with the sRGB tone curve; PDF/A always), outputIntent: profile name (embedded as the catalog's /GTS_PDFX output intent; a name that isn't a profile is only named, which pdfX1a and pdfX3 allow only with a registry and pdfX4 refuses; pdfX1a needs a CMYK one), outputCondition, outputConditionId (default: outputIntent), registry, trapped (/Trapped /True; /False when an output intent is written)} (PDF/A files keep their own output intent); default; every colour into the destination profile's model, CMYK or RGB, also colours of that model in another profile; only colours of the other model and Lab; those in the destination's model keep their numbers; grey stays grey; images are converted too, printer's marks are not; edit.colorSettings lists them; default: the document's profile for its colour mode; device colours; documents assigned a profile: edit.assignProfile; ICC-based colours: CMYK with the destination or document CMYK profile, RGB as sRGB, grey with the sRGB tone curve; PDF/A always; embedded as the catalog's /GTS_PDFX output intent; a name that isn't a profile is only named, which pdfX1a and pdfX3 allow only with a registry and pdfX4 refuses; pdfX1a needs a CMYK one; default: outputIntent; /Trapped /True; /False when an output intent is written; PDF/A files keep their own output intent
  - `path` file
  - `preserveEditing` boolean, on in Kition Vector Default: the native document as an embedded file, which document.open restores; choosing a standard turns it off, a standard refuses it
  - `preset` string, like Kition Vector Default; built-in or saved: pdf.preset.list
  - `security` object, {openPassword, permissionsPassword, printing: none|low|high, changes: none|pages|forms|comments|any, copy, screenReader, plaintextMetadata}
  - `standard` string, one of `none` | `pdfA2b` | `pdfX1a` | `pdfX3` | `pdfX4`, CMYK, grey and spot colours only: colours and images converted to output.destination or the CMYK output intent, untagged; transparency flattened with flattenerPreset; PDF 1.3; colours ICC-tagged; transparency flattened; PDF 1.3; transparency and layers kept; colours ICC-tagged; PDF 1.6 at most; PDF/X: a /GTS_PDFX output intent, by default the CMYK profile in effect, embedded; TrimBox, Trapped, GTS_PDFXVersion, title and dates; fonts embedded or outlined
  - `thumbnails` boolean
  - `viewAfterSaving` boolean
- `document.pdfSettings` (reads): Answers the PDF settings a preset gives with options applied and how they differ from it, without writing a file.
  - `includeDocument` boolean, default `false`
  - `preset` string
- `document.setup` (writes): Sets Document Setup options: units, bleed, outline images, font substitution highlighting, transparency grid, type options and language.
  - `backgroundContents` string, one of `transparent` | `white`, white: raster exports are white behind the art
  - `bleed` number or array or object
  - `discardWhiteOverprint` boolean
  - `exportText` string, one of `editable` | `appearance`, SVG text as text or as outlines
  - `flattenerPreset` string
  - `gridColors` string[]
  - `gridSize` string, one of `small` | `medium` | `large`
  - `highlightSubstitutedFonts` boolean
  - `highlightSubstitutedGlyphs` boolean
  - `language` string
  - `outlineImages` boolean, show images in Outline mode
  - `quotes` object, beside a language: only if they differ from the current ones
  - `simulatePaper` boolean
  - `smallCapsSize` number, percent
  - `subscript` object
  - `superscript` object
  - `typographersQuotes` boolean, typed straight quotes become the document's quotes
  - `units` string
- `file.newPresets` (reads): Answers the New Document presets by category (recent, saved, mobile, web, print and more) with their sizes.
  - `category` string, one of `Recent` | `Saved` | `Mobile` | `Web` | `Print` | `Film & Video` | `Art & Illustration` | `Branding` | `Social`
- `file.newPresets.save` (writes): Saves New Document settings as a user preset in the Saved category.
  - `name` string
  - `preset` string
- `file.newPresets.delete` (writes): Deletes a saved New Document preset.
  - `name` string
- `file.place.info` (reads): Answers what file.place would place from a file (size, resolution, colour mode, warnings, thumbnail) without placing it.
  - `crop` string
  - `page` integer
  - `password` string
  - `thumbnail` number, pixels
- `image.info` (reads): Answers an image object's link, colour mode, pixel size, resolution and placed size.
  - `id` integer or string, an id
- `file.place.queue` (reads): Loads the place cursor with up to 100 files so later clicks place them one by one.
  - `crop` string
  - `dxf` object
  - `files` array
  - `link` boolean
  - `page` integer
  - `paths` file[]
  - `template` boolean
  - `text` string
  - `thumbnail` number, pixels
- `links.check` (reads): Answers whether each linked file is where it was and whether it changed since it was read.
  - `ids` json[], [image or placed document ids] (default: every linked image and placed document); default: every linked image and placed document
- `links.update` (writes): Reads modified linked files again, keeping each object's bounds; answers what was updated and what is missing.
  - `ids` json[], [image or placed document ids] (default: the linked images whose file was modified or is showing its preview, and placed documents whose file was modified); default: the linked images whose file was modified or is showing its preview, and placed documents whose file was modified
- `links.updateChanged` (writes): Reads again every linked file that changed on disk since it was last seen. No parameters.
- `links.relink` (writes): Links images or placed documents to another file, or each to a same-named file in a folder.
  - `ids` json[], [image or placed document ids] (default: the selected ones; with folder and nothing selected, every missing link); default: the selected ones; with folder and nothing selected, every missing link
- `links.list` (reads): Answers every image and placed document as the Links panel lists them, filtered and sorted.
  - `show` string, one of `all` | `missing` | `modified` | `embedded`, default
  - `sort` string, one of `name` | `kind` | `status`
- `links.goTo` (writes): Selects a linked image or placed document and answers its bounds.
  - `id` integer or string, an id
- `links.embed` (writes): Embeds linked images (keeping their pixels) or turns placed documents into editable art, breaking the links.
  - `ids` json[], [image or placed document ids] (default: the selected linked ones); default: the selected linked ones
- `links.unembed` (writes): Writes an embedded image's pixels to a file and links the image to it.
  - `id` integer
  - `path` file
- `links.info` (reads): Answers an image's or placed document's Link Info: file, status, format, colour mode, size and effective resolution.
  - `id` integer or string, an id
- `links.placementOptions` (writes): Sets how linked art fits its bounds when the file is updated or relinked: preserve transforms, bounds, file size, fit or fill, with alignment.
  - `align` string, one of `topLeft` | `top` | `topRight` | `left` | `center` | `right` | `bottomLeft` | `bottom` | `bottomRight`, default; where the new art sits; not for bounds
  - `clip` boolean, default `false`, clip it to the old bounds where it is larger
  - `ids` json[], [image or placed document ids] (default: the selected ones); default: the selected ones
  - `preserve` string, one of `transforms` | `bounds` | `fileDimensions` | `fit` | `fill`, default
- `pdf.preset.list` (reads): Answers the PDF presets, built-in and saved, with their descriptions and settings. No parameters.
- `pdf.preset.save` (reads): Creates or changes a saved PDF preset from options; answers it.
  - `description` string
  - `name` string, default: a new "PDF Preset N"
  - `newName` string
  - `preset` string
- `pdf.preset.delete` (reads): Deletes a saved PDF preset (built-in ones stay).
  - `name` string
- `pdf.preset.export` (reads): Writes PDF presets as a .vcpdfpresets file, or answers its text.
  - `names` array, [preset names, built-in ones too] (default: every saved preset); default: every saved preset
  - `path` file
- `pdf.preset.import` (reads): Imports PDF presets from a .vcpdfpresets file.
  - `replace` boolean, default `false`, replace saved presets of the same names; else imported ones whose name is taken get a number
- `document.exportDxf` (writes): Writes the document as a DXF drawing with a version, unit, scale and colour depth, or answers the data.
  - `alterPaths` boolean, default `false`, every stroke as its filled outline
  - `artboard` integer, default `0`, the origin is its bottom-left corner
  - `colors` integer or boolean
  - `outlineText` boolean, default `false`
  - `path` file
  - `preserve` string, one of `appearance` | `editability`, default: type as outlines; strokes a CAD line can't draw as filled outlines; brush art; type as text; every stroke a line with its lineweight and dashes
  - `rasterFormat` string, one of `png` | `jpeg`, default; placed images, written next to the file
  - `scale` integer, default `1`, drawing units per unit
  - `scaleLineweights` boolean, default `false`
  - `selectedOnly` boolean, default `false`, the selected objects, in their layers
  - `unit` string
  - `useArtboards` string, one of `true` | `false`, one drawing per chosen artboard, artboards?/range?, holding the art over it: {stem}-{artboard}.dxf; the origin at the art's bounds
  - `version` string, one of `R12` | `R13` | `R14` | `2000` | `2004` | `2007` | `2010` | `2013` | `2018`
- `document.exportEps` (writes): Writes the document as EPS with a PostScript level, preview and transparency options, or answers the data.
  - `cmykPostScript` boolean, default `true`, RGB documents written in CMYK
  - `compatibleGradients` boolean, default `false`, stepped gradients at level 3 too
  - `embedFonts` boolean, default `true`, type is always written as outlines, so no fonts are needed
  - `flattener` object
  - `flattenerPreset` string, like medium; default; high, low or a saved preset: flattener.presets.list
  - `includeLinkedFiles` boolean, default `false`, the embedded document keeps linked images whole, not just their previews
  - `level` integer, one of `2` | `3`, default; PostScript language level: 3 writes smooth gradients and masks transparent image pixels out, 2 steps gradients and writes those pixels white
  - `overprints` string, one of `preserve` | `discard`, default
  - `path` file
  - `previewFormat` string, one of `none` | `tiffBw` | `tiffColor`, default: a TIFF preview other apps show
  - `selectedOnly` boolean, default `false`
  - `thumbnails` boolean, default `true`, a PNG thumbnail in the file
  - `transparentPreview` boolean, default `true`, else on white
  - `useArtboards` string, one of `true` | `false`, one file per chosen artboard, artboards?/range?, {stem}_{artboard}.eps, the bounding box the artboard; default: one file, the bounding box the visible art, y up from the first artboard's bottom-left corner
- `file.package` (writes): Packages the document with copies of its linked files and fonts into a folder, optionally relinking to the copies, and writes a report.
  - `copyFonts` boolean, default `true`, the fonts its type uses go in Fonts/; fonts whose licence doesn't allow embedding are left out
  - `copyLinks` boolean, default `true`
  - `folder` file
  - `linksFolder` boolean, default `true`, the linked files go in Links/, else next to the document
  - `name` string, default: "<document> Folder"
  - `relink` boolean, default `true`, the packaged document links to the copies
  - `report` boolean, default `true`, <document> Report.txt
- `slice.list` (reads): Answers the slices as laid out, numbered left to right and top to bottom, with their sources, rectangles and options. No parameters.
- `object.slice.create` (writes): Creates a user slice over a rectangle, as dragging with the Slice tool does.
  - `height` number
  - `width` number
  - `x` number
  - `y` number
- `object.slice.setRect` (writes): Moves or resizes a user slice.
  - `height` number
  - `id` integer
  - `width` number
  - `x` number
  - `y` number
- `object.slice.move` (writes): Moves slices by dx, dy (object slices move their objects).
  - `dx` number
  - `dy` number
  - `slices` array, default: the selected slices
- `object.slice.delete` (writes): Deletes user slices and releases object slices (their objects stay).
  - `slices` array, default: the selected slices
- `object.slice.select` (writes): Selects slices as the Slice Selection tool does, deselecting objects.
  - `slices` array, user slice ids or ids of objects with an object slice; none: deselect the slices
  - `toggle` boolean, Shift: add the unselected ones, drop the selected ones
- `print.setup` (writes): Sets the document's print settings: copies, artboards, media, orientation, scaling, tiling, marks, bleed, output and separations.

separations always keep them), flattenerPreset: "" (a flattener preset, built-in or saved: transparency is flattened before printing; empty: it prints live; PostScript defaults to medium)}, tileOrigin: {placed: false, x, y} (where the Print Tiling tool put the pages: print.tiling.set)}; 1-based tiles across then down; empty: all; pt the device can't print around the paper: the imageable area is inside it; as document.exportPdf, at the paper's scale; page information adds the tile and the ink; the document's bleed, document.setup; pt; one grey page per ink that prints; down mirrors; lpi, default 60; default C 15, M 75, Y 0, K 45, spots 45; 0.2–100; CMYK colours keep their values; the printer profile, an RGB or CMYK one: composite PDF colours are converted to it with the intent, separations separate with a CMYK one; empty: as they are; composite pages print as one image each, at the document's raster effects resolution; composite output; preserve writes them to overprint (/OP), simulate prints them as Overprint Preview shows them; separations always keep them; a flattener preset, built-in or saved: transparency is flattened before printing; empty: it prints live; PostScript defaults to medium; where the Print Tiling tool put the pages: print.tiling.set
- `print.preview` (reads): Answers the print layout the settings give: page count and each sheet's artboard, tile, size, orientation and scale.
  - `settings` object, over the document's
- `file.print` (writes): Prints the document by writing a print-ready PDF or PostScript file with the print settings.
  - `flattenerPreset` string, like medium; PostScript: the preset transparency is flattened with — high, low or a saved one, see flattener.presets.list
  - `format` string, one of `pdf` | `postscript`, default: a print-ready PDF; the default for a .ps path: a PostScript file with DSC comments, %%Pages, a page per sheet with its paper size, marks, separations with their ink and halftone screen, the fixed flatness, negatives
  - `level` integer, one of `3` | `2`, the PostScript language level
  - `path` file
  - `settings` object, over the document's
- `file.recovery.save` (writes): Writes a recovery copy of every modified document changed since its last copy. No parameters.
- `file.recovery.list` (reads): Answers the recovery copies in the store with their titles, paths, formats and whether they belong to open documents. No parameters.
- `file.recovery.restore` (writes): Opens recovery copies left by a crash as new modified documents titled with [Recovered].
  - `file` file
- `file.recovery.discard` (writes): Deletes recovery copies left by a crash.
  - `file` file
- `document.dxfInfo` (reads): Answers what a DXF drawing holds (version, units, layouts, layers, default scale) without opening it.
  - `path` file
- `document.exportForWeb` (writes): Writes an optimised GIF, JPEG or PNG for the web with a preset and settings (colours, dither, quality, size), or answers the data.
  - `antiAlias` string, one of `none` | `art` | `type`, default
  - `artboard` integer, default `0`, 0-based
  - `clipToArtboard` boolean, default `true`, the artboard; false: the art and the slices
  - `colorTable` object, kept when reducing; become transparent; become web-safe; colours as the preview's colors[].source
  - `colors` integer, default `128`, 2–256
  - `convertToSrgb` boolean, default `true`, PNG files say they are sRGB
  - `dither` string, one of `none` | `diffusion` | `pattern` | `noise`, default
  - `ditherAmount` integer, default `100`
  - `embedProfile` boolean, default `false`, sRGB profile
  - `format` string, one of `gif` | `jpg` | `png8` | `png24`, default
  - `interlaced` boolean, default `false`, gif/png8/png24
  - `jpg` object
  - `lossy` integer, default `0`, 0–100, gif
  - `matte` string
  - `metadata` string, one of `none` | `copyright` | `contact` | `all`, default; File Info written as PNG text, a GIF or JPEG comment
  - `optimized` boolean, default `true`
  - `output` string, one of `images` | `html`, default; an HTML page placing the image or slices, <stem>.html
  - `path` file
  - `preset` string
  - `progressive` boolean, default `false`
  - `slices` string, one of `all` | `selected` | `none`, default; one image per slice: images/<slice name>.<ext>
  - `transparency` boolean, default `true`, gif/png8/png24
  - `webSnap` integer, default `0`, 0–100 %: colours that close to a web-safe one become it
  - `width` number
- `document.exportForWeb.preview` (reads): Answers what Save for Web would write: file size, colours and download time, optionally with the image data.
  - `image` boolean, default `false`, also the optimised file as dataBase64
  - `kbps` number, default `56.6`, connection speed for the download time
  - `slice` integer, 1-based, from slice.list; default the whole image
- `webExport.settings` (reads): Reads or changes the remembered Save for Web settings.
  - `preset` string
  - `reset` boolean, default `false`
- `webExport.presets.list` (reads): Answers the Save for Web presets, built-in and saved, with their settings. No parameters.
- `webExport.presets.save` (reads): Creates or changes a saved Save for Web preset.
  - `name` string
  - `newName` string
  - `preset` string
  - `settings` object
- `webExport.presets.delete` (reads): Deletes a saved Save for Web preset.
  - `name` string
- `assets.remove` (writes): Removes assets from the Asset Export panel (their art stays).
  - `assets` array
- `assets.rename` (writes): Renames an asset, which names its exported files.
  - `asset` integer, an id
  - `name` string
- `assets.list` (reads): Answers the Asset Export panel's assets with their objects and bounds. No parameters.
- `assets.export` (writes): Exports each asset's art, cropped to it, in every format row of the export settings, to a folder or zip.
  - `antiAlias` string, one of `none` | `art` | `type`
  - `assets` array, default all
  - `folder` file
  - `formats` object[]
  - `openLocation` boolean
  - `prefix` string
  - `preset` string
  - `settings` object
  - `subfolders` boolean
  - `zip` boolean
- `assets.settings.set` (writes): Changes the export settings the Asset Export panel and Export for Screens share.
  - `antiAlias` string, one of `none` | `art` | `type`
  - `formats` object[]
  - `prefix` string
  - `preset` string, one of `mobile` | `density` | ``
  - `settings` object
  - `subfolders` boolean
- `css.selection` (reads): Answers CSS rules for the selected objects (fills, strokes, type, opacity, optionally positions and sizes) in a unit.
  - `dimensions` boolean, default `true`, width, height
  - `ids` array, default: the selection
  - `position` boolean, default `false`, position: absolute, left and top from the artboard's top-left
  - `rasterize` boolean, default `false`, art CSS can't describe as background-image: url(<class>.png), its picture, which css.export writes
  - `units` string, one of `px` | `pt` | `mm` | `cm` | `in`
  - `unnamed` boolean, default `true`, unnamed objects too, classes named after their kind; false: named objects only
- `css.generate` (reads): Answers CSS rules for every object in the document. No parameters.
- `css.export` (writes): Writes CSS for the selection or all objects to a file, optionally rasterizing pictures its rules refer to.
  - `path` file
  - `scope` string, one of `selection` | `all`, default selection; ids? picks the objects
- `print.presets.list` (reads): Answers the print presets, [Default] first, with their settings and differences from it. No parameters.
- `print.presets.save` (reads): Creates or changes a saved print preset.
  - `name` string, default: a new "Print Preset N"
  - `newName` string
  - `preset` string
  - `settings` object, over it
- `print.presets.delete` (reads): Deletes a saved print preset ([Default] stays).
  - `name` string
- `print.presets.export` (reads): Writes print presets as a .vcprintpresets file, or answers its text.
  - `names` array, [preset names, [Default] too] (default: every saved preset); default: every saved preset
  - `path` file
- `print.presets.import` (reads): Imports print presets from a .vcprintpresets file.
  - `replace` boolean, default `false`, replace saved presets of the same names; else imported ones whose name is taken get a number
- `print.tiling.set` (writes): Places the print tiling origin (the first page's imageable area) or resets it.
  - `artboard` integer, 0-based: the artboard it is measured from; default the printed artboard containing origin, else the first; ignored with artboards: ignore
  - `origin` number[], document point: the top-left corner of the first page's imageable area
- `print.tiling` (reads): Answers the print pages as Show Print Tiling draws them, with their positions and numbers.
  - `settings` object, over the document's
- `plugin.list` (reads): Answers the installed WebAssembly plug-ins (filters and live effects) with their parameters. No parameters.
- `plugin.info` (reads): Answers one plug-in's entry, manifest, defaults and last error.
  - `id` integer or string, an id
- `plugin.run` (writes): Runs an object-filter plug-in with parameters on the selected paths.
  - `id` integer or string, an id
  - `ids` json[], [..] (default: the selection); default: the selection
  - `params` object, the plug-in's parameters; or give them as top-level keys; missing ones take their defaults, see plugin.info
- `plugin.install` (reads): Validates and installs a WebAssembly plug-in for this session from a file or bytes.
  - `path` file, a .wasm file (desktop) | dataBase64: the module (+ name?: shown as its source); desktop; + name?: shown as its source
  - `replace` boolean, true: a plug-in with the same id is replaced
- `plugin.remove` (reads): Uninstalls a plug-in; its live effects then leave the geometry as it is.
  - `id` integer or string, an id
- `path.mirrorCut` (writes): Cuts the selected art along an axis and mirrors the kept side onto the other, as one undo step.
  - `axis` string, one of `vertical` | `horizontal` | `free`, vertical
  - `from` number[]
  - `keep` string, one of `left` | `right` | `top` | `bottom`, the side kept; default left, or top for a horizontal-ish axis
  - `to` number[], free: the axis through both; vertical/horizontal: the axis through `from`, default the selection's centre
- `path.lineCut` (writes): Splits the selected paths along the line through two points, extended across the art; answers the pieces.
  - `from` number[]
  - `to` number[]
- `path.rectCut` (writes): Crops the selected paths to a rectangle as real geometry (not a clipping mask).
  - `rect` array, [x, y, width, height]
- `perspective.grid.get` (reads): Answers the document's perspective grid model, its Define Grid fields and the station point. No parameters.
- `perspective.grid.define` (writes): Defines the perspective grid as the Define Grid dialog does: preset, kind, units, scale, gridlines, viewing angle and distance, horizon and colours.
  - `angle` number
  - `distance` number
  - `gridline` number
  - `groundColor` string, like #rrggbb
  - `horizonHeight` number
  - `kind` integer, one of `1` | `2` | `3`
  - `leftColor` string
  - `name` string
  - `opacity` number
  - `rightColor` string
  - `scale` array, [artboard, real world]
  - `thirdVp` number[]
  - `units` string
- `perspective.presets.list` (reads): Answers the perspective grid presets, built-in and saved. No parameters.
- `perspective.presets.save` (reads): Creates or changes a saved perspective grid preset.
  - `name` string, default: a new "Perspective Preset N"
  - `newName` string
  - `preset` string
- `perspective.presets.delete` (reads): Deletes a saved perspective grid preset.
  - `name` string
- `perspective.presets.export` (reads): Writes perspective grid presets as a .vcperspective file, or answers its text.
  - `names` array, [preset names, built-in ones too] (default: every saved preset); default: every saved preset
  - `path` file
- `perspective.presets.import` (reads): Imports perspective grid presets from a .vcperspective file.
  - `replace` boolean, default `false`, replace saved presets of the same names; else imported ones whose name is taken get a number
- `perspective.widget.options` (reads): Shows or hides the Plane Switching Widget and sets its corner; with no params answers the settings.
  - `position` string, one of `topLeft` | `topRight` | `bottomLeft` | `bottomRight`
  - `show` boolean
- `perspective.grid.lock` (writes): Locks, unlocks or toggles the perspective grid's widgets; not an undo step.
  - `on` boolean
- `perspective.grid.lockStation` (writes): Locks, unlocks or toggles the station point so dragging a vanishing point turns the viewing angle.
  - `on` boolean
- `perspective.grid.snap` (writes): Turns snapping to the perspective gridlines on, off or toggles it.
  - `on` boolean
- `perspective.grid.rulers` (writes): Shows, hides or toggles the perspective grid's ruler.
  - `on` boolean

### File > Document Setup

- `document.setUnits` (writes): Sets the document's units, which every length the editor shows and reads uses; drawing coordinates passed to commands stay in points.
  - `units` string, one of `Points` | `Picas` | `Inches` | `Millimeters` | `Centimeters` | `Pixels` | `Feet & Inches` | `Meters` | `Yards` | `Feet`

### Edit

- `edit.undo` (writes): Undoes the last step in a scope (the person's or the agent's; default the caller's), leaving the other scope's later steps in place.
  - `scope` string, one of `person` | `agent`
- `edit.redo` (writes): Redoes the last undone step in a scope (the person's or the agent's; default the caller's).
  - `scope` string, one of `person` | `agent`
- `edit.cut` (writes): Removes the selection and puts it on the kit's clipboard (with the Artboard tool chosen, the active artboard and its art). No parameters.
- `edit.copy` (reads): Copies the selection to the kit's clipboard without changing the document (with the Artboard tool chosen, the active artboard and its art). No parameters.
- `edit.paste` (writes): Pastes the clipboard's objects and the resources they use, centred on center or offset by dx/dy; answers the new ids and any resources added, merged or renamed. Use pasteInPlace to keep their positions.
  - `center` number[]
  - `dx` number
  - `dy` number
  - `swatchConflict` string or object
- `edit.pasteInFront` (writes): Pastes the clipboard in place just above the top selected object, or on top of the current layer; answers the new ids.
  - `artboard` integer, a position counted from 0 (the first is 0); the active artboard: the objects go where they were on the artboard they were copied from, on this one
  - `swatchConflict` string or object
- `edit.pasteInBack` (writes): Pastes the clipboard in place just below the bottom selected object, or at the bottom of the current layer; answers the new ids.
  - `artboard` integer, a position counted from 0 (the first is 0); as edit.pasteInFront
  - `swatchConflict` string or object
- `edit.pasteInPlace` (writes): Pastes the clipboard at the exact positions the objects were copied from; answers the new ids.
  - `artboard` integer, a position counted from 0 (the first is 0); as edit.pasteInFront
  - `swatchConflict` string or object
- `edit.pasteOnAllArtboards` (writes): Pastes a copy of the clipboard on every artboard at the offset the objects had to their original artboard; answers the new ids.
  - `swatchConflict` string or object
- `edit.clear` (writes): Deletes the objects ids, else the selection (direct-selected anchors, else whole objects, else selected ruler guides).
  - `ids` array
- `edit.colorSettings` (reads): Sets the RGB and CMYK working spaces, rendering intent and black point compensation; answers them with the available profiles.
  - `bpc` boolean
  - `cmyk` string
  - `intent` string, one of `perceptual` | `relative` | `saturation` | `absolute`
  - `rgb` string
- `edit.assignProfile` (writes): Tags the document with RGB and/or CMYK profiles without changing colour numbers.
  - `cmyk` string or null
  - `rgb` string or null
- `edit.findReplace` (writes): Finds and replaces text in every type object (or ids), optionally matching case and whole words; answers the count replaced.
  - `find` string
  - `ids` array
  - `matchCase` boolean, default `false`
  - `replace` string, like
  - `wholeWord` boolean, default `false`
- `edit.findNext` (reads): Selects the next type object containing find, after the selected one; answers its id or null.
  - `find` string
  - `matchCase` boolean
  - `wholeWord` boolean
- `edit.pasteWithoutFormatting` (writes): Pastes like edit.paste, but pasted text takes the default character style and drops its own styles.
  - `center` number[]
  - `dx` number
  - `dy` number
  - `swatchConflict` string or object

### Edit > Edit Colors

- `recolor.apply` (writes): Recolours the selection in one undo step by a map of colour rows (from keys or hex to a new colour), with a tint method, an optional swatch library to snap to and a colour group to rewrite.
  - `group` string
  - `includeImages` boolean, default `true`
  - `includePatterns` boolean, default `true`
  - `limitTo` string
  - `map` array or object
  - `method` string, one of `exact` | `preserveTints` | `scaleTints` | `tintsShades` | `hueShift`, default; how a row's colours take its new colour, relative to the row's darkest, average or most saturated colour
  - `rename` string
- `edit.colors.invert` (writes): Inverts the colours of the selection or ids in fills, strokes, text, meshes, embedded images and pattern tiles.
  - `fill` boolean, default `true`
  - `ids` array
  - `includeImages` boolean, default `true`
  - `includePatterns` boolean, default `true`
  - `stroke` boolean, default `true`
- `edit.colors.toCMYK` (writes): Converts the colours of the selection or ids to CMYK; answers how many changed.
  - `fill` boolean
  - `ids` array
  - `includeImages` boolean
  - `includePatterns` boolean
  - `stroke` boolean
- `edit.colors.toGrayscale` (writes): Converts the colours of the selection or ids to greyscale; answers how many changed.
  - `fill` boolean
  - `ids` array
  - `includeImages` boolean
  - `includePatterns` boolean
  - `stroke` boolean
- `edit.colors.toRGB` (writes): Converts the colours of the selection or ids to RGB; answers how many changed.
  - `fill` boolean
  - `ids` array
  - `includeImages` boolean
  - `includePatterns` boolean
  - `stroke` boolean
- `edit.colors.saturate` (writes): Increases or decreases the saturation of the selection's colours by an intensity percentage; answers how many changed.
  - `fill` boolean
  - `ids` array
  - `includeImages` boolean
  - `includePatterns` boolean
  - `intensity` integer, -100 to 100; %
  - `stroke` boolean
- `edit.colors.adjustBalance` (writes): Shifts the selection's colours by per-channel amounts in RGB, CMYK, grey or global tint mode; answers how many changed.
  - `convert` boolean, default `false`, true: the results stay in the adjusted model; false: each colour keeps its own
  - `fill` boolean
  - `g` number
  - `gray` integer, -100 to 100; % added per channel, default 0; `tint` is global mode: it shifts the tints of colours and gradient stops linked to global and spot swatches, which stay linked, and leaves other colours and images alone; one of several alternative parameters
  - `ids` array
  - `includeImages` boolean
  - `includePatterns` boolean
  - `k` integer, -100 to 100; % added per channel, default 0; `tint` is global mode: it shifts the tints of colours and gradient stops linked to global and spot swatches, which stay linked, and leaves other colours and images alone; one of several alternative parameters
  - `m` number
  - `mode` string, one of `rgb` | `cmyk` | `gray` | `global`, default: from the channels given
  - `r` number
  - `stroke` boolean
  - `tint` integer, -100 to 100; % added per channel, default 0; `tint` is global mode: it shifts the tints of colours and gradient stops linked to global and spot swatches, which stay linked, and leaves other colours and images alone; one of several alternative parameters
  - `y` number
- `edit.colors.blendFrontToBack` (writes): Grades the fills of three or more selected objects between the frontmost and backmost colours. No parameters.
- `edit.colors.blendHorizontally` (writes): Grades the fills of three or more selected objects between the leftmost and rightmost colours. No parameters.
- `edit.colors.blendVertically` (writes): Grades the fills of three or more selected objects between the topmost and bottommost colours. No parameters.
- `edit.colors.overprintBlack` (writes): Makes the black fills and/or strokes of the selection overprint (or stops them), optionally including rich and spot blacks.
  - `fill` boolean, default `true`
  - `ids` array
  - `includeCmyBlacks` boolean, default `false`
  - `includeSpotBlacks` boolean, default `false`
  - `percentage` integer, default `100`
  - `remove` boolean, default `false`
  - `stroke` boolean, default `true`

### File > Export

- `document.exportForScreens` (writes): Exports each chosen artboard or asset in one or more formats and sizes (as the Export for Screens dialog does), to a folder or a zip; answers the files written. Remembers the settings in the document.
  - `antiAlias` string, one of `none` | `art` | `type`, raster rows without their own
  - `artboards` integer[]
  - `assets` array, instead of artboards: each asset's art alone, cropped to its bounds and named after the asset; see assets.list
  - `folder` file
  - `formats` object[], [{format: png|png8|jpg|webp|gif|svg|svgz|pdf, scale?: 1 | "2x" | "100w" | "100h" | "72ppi", width?: px | height?: px | ppi? (raster only; width, then height, then ppi win over scale), suffix?: (raster default: @2x, @100w, @100h, none at 1x; vector formats drop size suffixes), folder?: (its sub-folder), quality?: (jpg 0–100), …the format's options (antiAlias, background, preset (pdf)…)}]; raster only; width, then height, then ppi win over scale; raster default: @2x, @100w, @100h, none at 1x; vector formats drop size suffixes; its sub-folder; jpg 0–100; antiAlias, background, preset (pdf)…
  - `fullDocument` boolean, default `false`, one file per format instead: a PDF of every artboard, other formats the bounds of all visible art, named after the document
  - `includeBleed` boolean, default `false`, artboards grown by the document's bleed
  - `openLocation` boolean
  - `prefix` string
  - `preset` string, one of `mobile` | `density`
  - `settings` object, rows' own options win
  - `subfolders` boolean, default `false`, each row's files in a sub-folder: its folder, else its size for raster (1x, 2x, 100w…) or its format (SVG, PDF)
  - `zip` boolean, default `false`, one store-only .zip of every file: no folder → {name, dataBase64, bytes, files: [name…]}; with a folder it is written there → {path, bytes, files}

### Object > Transform

- `object.move` (writes): Moves the selection by dx, dy points, optionally as a copy.
  - `copy` boolean
  - `dx` number
  - `dy` number
  - `patterns` boolean, Transform Patterns: pattern fills and strokes transform with the art; default: prefs transformPatternTiles
- `object.rotate` (writes): Rotates the selection by an angle (or to an absolute angle) about an origin, default its centre, optionally as a copy; answers the ids.
  - `absolute` boolean, angle is the bounding box's new angle, not an amount
  - `angle` number, degrees; counter-clockwise
  - `copy` boolean
  - `origin` number[], default: the bounding box centre
  - `patterns` boolean, Transform Patterns: pattern fills and strokes transform with the art; default: prefs transformPatternTiles
- `object.scale` (writes): Scales the selection by sx and sy percent about an origin, optionally as a copy and scaling strokes, corners and patterns.
  - `copy` boolean
  - `corners` boolean, Scale Corners: corner radii scale
  - `origin` number[]
  - `patterns` boolean, Transform Patterns: pattern fills and strokes transform with the art; default: prefs transformPatternTiles
  - `strokes` boolean, Scale Strokes & Effects: stroke weights, dashes and effect distances scale; off keeps them, type strokes included
  - `sx` number, percent
  - `sy` number, percent
- `object.reflect` (writes): Mirrors the selection across a vertical, horizontal or angled axis through an origin, optionally as a copy.
  - `axis` string or number
  - `copy` boolean
  - `origin` number[]
  - `patterns` boolean, Transform Patterns: pattern fills and strokes transform with the art; default: prefs transformPatternTiles
- `object.shear` (writes): Shears the selection by an angle along a horizontal or vertical axis through an origin, optionally as a copy.
  - `angle` number, degrees
  - `axis` string, one of `horizontal` | `vertical`
  - `copy` boolean
  - `origin` number[]
  - `patterns` boolean, Transform Patterns: pattern fills and strokes transform with the art; default: prefs transformPatternTiles
- `object.transformAgain` (writes): Repeats the last move, scale, rotate, reflect, shear or transform on the current selection. No parameters.
- `object.transformEach` (writes): Scales, moves, rotates and reflects each selected object about its own reference point (optionally randomised or as copies), as Transform Each does.
  - `copy` boolean
  - `corners` boolean, Scale Corners; both default to the preferences
  - `moveH` number, points
  - `moveV` number, points; down = +
  - `patterns` boolean, Transform Patterns; default: prefs transformPatternTiles
  - `random` boolean
  - `reference` integer, 0 to 8; 9-point grid, 4 = centre
  - `reflectX` boolean, flip vertically
  - `reflectY` boolean, flip horizontally
  - `rotate` number, degrees; counter-clockwise
  - `scaleH` number, percent; 100
  - `scaleV` number, percent; 100
  - `seed` integer
  - `strokes` boolean, Scale Strokes & Effects
- `object.resetBoundingBox` (writes): Squares the bounding box of rotated selected objects back to the page without changing their geometry. No parameters.

### Object > Arrange

- `object.arrange.bringToFront` (writes): Moves the selected objects to the top of their layer's stacking order. No parameters.
- `object.arrange.bringForward` (writes): Moves the selected objects one step up in the stacking order. No parameters.
- `object.arrange.sendBackward` (writes): Moves the selected objects one step down in the stacking order. No parameters.
- `object.arrange.sendToBack` (writes): Moves the selected objects to the bottom of their layer's stacking order. No parameters.
- `object.arrange.sendToCurrentLayer` (writes): Moves the selected objects to the top of the current layer. No parameters.

### Object

- `object.group` (writes): Groups the selected objects into one group in place and answers the group's id. No parameters.
- `object.ungroup` (writes): Ungroups the selected groups, leaving their children selected in the same stacking position. No parameters.
- `object.unlockAll` (writes): Unlocks every locked object in the document and selects them. No parameters.
- `object.showAll` (writes): Shows every hidden object in the document and selects them. No parameters.
- `effect.expandAppearance` (writes): Expands each object's appearance into plain objects: every fill and stroke becomes its own object and geometry effects are baked in.
  - `ids` json[], [..]
  - `target` string, one of `object` | `contents`
- `object.rasterize` (writes): Replaces the selected objects with an embedded raster image at a resolution, background, anti-aliasing and colour model.
  - `addAround` number, points; 0–1000; one of several alternative parameters
  - `antiAlias` string or boolean
  - `background` string
  - `clippingMask` boolean, a clip group with the art's outline
  - `colorModel` string, one of `rgb` | `cmyk` | `grayscale` | `bitmap`
  - `padding` number, points; 0–1000; one of several alternative parameters
  - `ppi` number
- `object.createObjectMosaic` (writes): Builds a group of rectangles coloured by the selected image's tile colours (a mosaic), optionally deleting the image.
  - `deleteRaster` boolean
  - `gray` boolean
  - `height` number, new size in pt; default the image's
  - `width` number
- `object.cropImage` (writes): Crops the selected embedded image to a rectangle, its artboard or its non-transparent pixels.
  - `rect` number[]
- `object.createTrimMarks` (writes): Draws trim marks around the selection or every artboard, in Roman or Japanese style.
  - `allArtboards` boolean, default: true when nothing is selected
  - `bleed` number, points; 8.5, japanese
  - `length` number, points; 18
  - `offset` number, points; 9, roman
  - `style` string, one of `roman` | `japanese`, default: the japaneseCropMarks preference; japanese: double lines at the trim and bleed edges plus centre marks
  - `weight` number, points; 0.3
- `object.mesh.create` (writes): Converts the selected filled paths into gradient meshes of rows by columns, flat or highlighted at the centre or edge.
  - `appearance` string, one of `flat` | `center` | `edge`
  - `at` number[]
  - `cols` integer, 4
  - `highlight` number, percent; 100
  - `ids` array
  - `rows` integer, 4
- `object.mesh.expand` (writes): Replaces the selected gradient meshes with groups of flat-coloured pieces; answers the ids. No parameters.
- `object.makePixelPerfect` (writes): Snaps each selected object's edges to the pixel grid and rounds stroke weights.
  - `ids` array
- `object.flattenTransparency` (writes): Flattens transparency in the selected art into opaque vector and raster pieces with a flattener preset or options.
  - `antiAlias` boolean
  - `balance` integer, 0 to 100; raster/vector balance; 0 rasterizes everything
  - `clipComplexRegions` boolean
  - `gradientPpi` integer, 1 to 2400; areas only gradients and meshes reach
  - `ids` array
  - `lineArtPpi` integer, 1 to 2400
  - `options` object
  - `preserveAlpha` boolean, composite over nothing instead of white
  - `preserveOverprints` boolean, areas showing one paint keep its colour and overprint; false clears overprints
  - `preset` string
  - `strokesToOutlines` boolean
  - `textToOutlines` boolean
- `object.expand` (writes): Expands the selected objects, fills and/or strokes into plain art: type to outlines, live shapes to paths, effects baked, blends and envelopes to their content.
  - `fill` boolean, default `true`, gradient fills → `gradient` art
  - `gradient` string, one of `objects` | `mesh`, default: `steps` solid strips, concentric ellipses for radial gradients; a gradient mesh
  - `object` boolean, default `true`, type → outlines, live shapes → paths, effects baked, blends → groups of their steps, envelopes → their distorted content, placed documents → editable copies of their art, as placing the file without link gives, its symbols, patterns, swatches and images joining the document
  - `steps` integer, 1 to 1000; 255
  - `stroke` boolean, default `true`, strokes → filled outlines
- `object.vectorHalftone` (writes): Converts the selected art into a vector halftone of dots, lines or shapes at a frequency and angle, mono or CMYK.
  - `angle` number, degrees; 45; CMYK: the black screen's, cyan −30°, magenta +30°, yellow −45° from it
  - `clip` boolean, default `true`, clip the dots to the art's outline
  - `color` string
  - `frequency` number
  - `invert` boolean, dots for light tones
  - `keepOriginal` boolean, default `false`
  - `mode` string, one of `mono` | `cmyk`, mono
  - `shape` string, one of `circle` | `ellipse` | `square` | `diamond` | `line`, circle

### Object > Lock

- `object.lock` (writes): Locks the selected objects so they cannot be selected or edited until unlocked. No parameters.
- `object.lock.above` (writes): Locks the objects in the same layer that are above and overlap the selection; answers the count. No parameters.
- `object.lock.otherLayers` (writes): Locks every layer that holds no selected object; answers the count. No parameters.

### Object > Hide

- `object.hide` (writes): Hides the selected objects; object.showAll shows them again. No parameters.
- `object.hide.above` (writes): Hides the objects in the same layer that are above and overlap the selection; answers the count. No parameters.
- `object.hide.otherLayers` (writes): Hides every layer that holds no selected object; answers the count. No parameters.

### Object > Compound Path

- `object.compoundPath.make` (writes): Combines the selected paths into one compound path whose overlaps make holes. No parameters.
- `object.compoundPath.release` (writes): Splits the selected compound paths back into separate paths. No parameters.

### Object > Clipping Mask

- `object.clippingMask.make` (writes): Makes the topmost selected path, compound path or text clip the other selected objects into a clip group; answers the group's id. No parameters.
- `object.clippingMask.release` (writes): Turns the selected clip groups into plain groups, keeping their clipping path as an ordinary object. No parameters.
- `object.clippingMask.editContents` (reads): Selects the clipped art inside the selected clip groups, without changing them; answers how many objects are selected. No parameters.
- `object.clippingMask.editMask` (reads): Selects the clipping paths of the selected clip groups, without changing them; answers how many are selected. No parameters.

### Window > Align

- `object.align` (writes): Aligns the selected objects horizontally and/or vertically to the selection, the artboard or the key object, using preview or geometric bounds.
  - `bounds` string, one of `preview` | `geometric`, default: the Use Preview Bounds preference; preview bounds take in strokes
  - `horizontal` string, one of `left` | `center` | `right`
  - `to` string, one of `selection` | `artboard` | `key`, default: the key object when the selection has one, select.key, else the selection
  - `vertical` string, one of `top` | `center` | `bottom`
- `object.distribute` (writes): Distributes the selected objects evenly by their left, centre or right (or top, centre or bottom) edges.
  - `bounds` string, one of `preview` | `geometric`, default: the Use Preview Bounds preference; preview bounds take in strokes
  - `horizontal` string, one of `left` | `center` | `right`
  - `vertical` string, one of `top` | `center` | `bottom`
- `object.distributeSpacing` (writes): Spaces the selected objects evenly along an axis, or by a fixed spacing from the key object.
  - `axis` string, one of `horizontal` | `vertical`
  - `bounds` string, one of `preview` | `geometric`, default: the Use Preview Bounds preference; preview bounds take in strokes
  - `spacing` number, points; the key object, select.key, stays put and the others are spaced from it

### Object > Shape

- `object.expandShape` (writes): Converts the selected live shapes (rectangles, ellipses, polygons with corner widgets) into plain editable paths. No parameters.
- `object.shape.convertToShape` (writes): Turns selected paths that are rectangles or axis-aligned ellipses into live shapes; answers how many converted. No parameters.

### Object > Path

- `path.reverse` (writes): Reverses the direction of the selected or given paths, or sets every subpath clockwise or counter-clockwise.
  - `ids` array
  - `reversed` boolean, true: every subpath runs counter-clockwise on screen, false: clockwise, the Attributes panel's Reverse Path Direction On / Off; omitted: flip each path
- `path.join` (writes): Joins two open paths at their nearest (or chosen) ends into one path, or closes a single open path.
  - `ends` string[], which end of each path to join, as the Pen joins them; default: the nearest pair
  - `ids` string[], default: the selected paths
- `path.average` (writes): Moves the direct-selected anchors to their average position horizontally, vertically or both.
  - `axis` string, one of `horizontal` | `vertical` | `both`
- `path.removeAnchors` (writes): Removes the direct-selected anchors without opening their paths, refitting the curves. No parameters.
- `object.path.outlineStroke` (writes): Replaces the selected stroked paths with filled outlines of their strokes; answers the new ids. No parameters.
- `object.path.offsetPath` (writes): Adds offset copies of the selected paths, grown (or inset for negative offset) with the chosen joins; answers the new ids.
  - `joins` string, one of `miter` | `round` | `bevel`
  - `miterLimit` integer, default `4`
  - `offset` number, points; negative insets
- `object.path.simplify` (writes): Reduces the anchors of the selected paths within a tolerance, keeping corners; answers anchor counts before and after.
  - `cornerAngle` number, degrees; 30
  - `straightLines` boolean
  - `tolerance` number, points; 1
- `object.path.addAnchorPoints` (writes): Adds an anchor midway along every segment of the selected paths without changing their shape. No parameters.
- `object.path.divideObjectsBelow` (writes): Cuts the objects below with the selected path, which is removed; answers the resulting ids. No parameters.
- `object.path.splitIntoGrid` (writes): Splits each selected shape into a grid of rectangles with rows, columns and gutters; answers the new ids.
  - `columns` integer, default `2`
  - `gutter` number, points; 12
  - `rows` integer, default `2`
- `object.path.cleanUp` (writes): Deletes stray points, unpainted objects and empty text paths from the document; answers how many were removed.
  - `emptyTextPaths` boolean, default `true`
  - `strayPoints` boolean, default `true`
  - `unpaintedObjects` boolean, default `true`

### Select

- `select.all` (reads): Selects every unlocked, visible object (or all text while the Type tool edits) and answers the count. No parameters.
- `select.allOnArtboard` (reads): Selects every object on the active (or given) artboard.
  - `artboard` integer, a position counted from 0 (the first is 0)
- `select.none` (reads): Clears the selection, deselecting every object, anchor and guide. No parameters.
- `select.reselect` (reads): Repeats the last Select Same or Select Object command with the current selection. No parameters.
- `select.inverse` (reads): Selects every object that is not selected and deselects the others. No parameters.
- `select.nextAbove` (reads): Selects the next object above the selected one in the stacking order. No parameters.
- `select.nextBelow` (reads): Selects the next object below the selected one in the stacking order. No parameters.
- `select.save` (writes): Saves the current selection in the document under a name so select.recall can restore it; answers the name.
  - `name` string
- `select.recall` (reads): Selects the objects of a saved selection (deleted ones are skipped); answers the count.
  - `name` string
- `select.editSaved` (reads): Renames or deletes saved selections in one undo step.
  - `delete` boolean
  - `name` string
  - `newName` string

### Select > Same

- `select.same.fillColor` (reads): Selects every object filled with the first selected object's fill colour (tints of the same global swatch included). No parameters.
- `select.same.strokeColor` (reads): Selects every object stroked with the first selected object's stroke colour. No parameters.
- `select.same.strokeWeight` (reads): Selects every object with the first selected object's stroke weight. No parameters.
- `select.same.fillAndStroke` (reads): Selects every object with both the first selected object's fill and stroke colours. No parameters.
- `select.same.opacity` (reads): Selects every object with the first selected object's opacity. No parameters.
- `select.same.blendingMode` (reads): Selects every object with the first selected object's blending mode. No parameters.
- `select.same.appearance` (reads): Selects every object with the same appearance stack as the first selected object. No parameters.
- `select.same.shapeType` (reads): Selects every live shape of the same kind as the first selected one (rectangles, ellipses, polygons). No parameters.
- `select.same.graphicStyle` (reads): Selects every object linked to the graphic style the first selected object is linked to. No parameters.
- `select.same.appearanceAttribute` (reads): Selects every object sharing one appearance attribute (a fill, stroke or effect) with the first selected object.
  - `item` integer
- `select.same.symbolInstance` (reads): Selects every instance of the symbol the first selected instance uses; answers the count. No parameters.
- `select.same.fontFamily` (reads): Selects every type object in the first selected type's font family; answers the count. No parameters.
- `select.same.fontFamilyStyle` (reads): Selects every type object in the first selected type's font family and style; answers the count. No parameters.
- `select.same.fontFamilyStyleSize` (reads): Selects every type object with the first selected type's font family, style and size; answers the count. No parameters.
- `select.same.fontSize` (reads): Selects every type object with the first selected type's font size; answers the count. No parameters.
- `select.same.textFillColor` (reads): Selects every type object with the first selected type's text fill colour; answers the count. No parameters.
- `select.same.textStrokeColor` (reads): Selects every type object with the first selected type's text stroke colour; answers the count. No parameters.

### Select > Object

- `select.object.allOnSameLayers` (reads): Selects every object on the layers the selected objects are on. No parameters.
- `select.object.clippingMasks` (reads): Selects every clipping path in the document. No parameters.
- `select.object.textObjects` (reads): Selects every type object in the document. No parameters.
- `select.object.strayPoints` (reads): Selects every stray point (a path with a single anchor), usually to delete them. No parameters.
- `select.object.openPaths` (reads): Selects every open path in the document. No parameters.
- `select.object.directionHandles` (reads): Direct-selects every anchor of the selected paths so all their handles show; answers the anchor count. No parameters.
- `select.object.pointText` (reads): Selects every point type object; answers the count. No parameters.
- `select.object.areaText` (reads): Selects every area type object; answers the count. No parameters.
- `select.object.brushStrokes` (reads): Selects every path with a brush applied to its stroke; answers the count. No parameters.
- `select.object.bristleBrushStrokes` (reads): Selects every path with a bristle brush on its stroke; answers the count. No parameters.
- `select.object.slices` (reads): Selects every user and object slice; answers the count. No parameters.

### Window > Magic Wand

- `magicWand.set` (reads): Changes the Magic Wand settings (which attributes to compare and their tolerances) and answers the settings; affects only select.magicWand.
  - `blendingMode` boolean
  - `fillColor` boolean
  - `fillTolerance` integer
  - `opacity` number
  - `opacityTolerance` number, percent
  - `reset` boolean
  - `strokeColor` boolean
  - `strokeTolerance` integer
  - `strokeWeight` boolean
  - `weightTolerance` number, points

### Window > Transparency

- `transparency.set` (writes): Sets opacity, blend mode, isolation and knockout of ids or the selection (or of one appearance item), as the Transparency panel does.
  - `blend` string
  - `isolate` boolean
  - `item` integer or null
  - `knockout` string or boolean
  - `knockoutShape` boolean
  - `opacity` integer, 0 to 100
- `transparency.makeOpacityMask` (writes): Makes the topmost selected object the opacity mask of the others (grouped if several); a single object gets an empty mask and enters mask editing.
  - `clip` boolean
  - `ids` array
  - `invert` boolean
- `transparency.releaseOpacityMask` (writes): Releases the opacity masks of the selection or ids, putting the mask art back above each masked object. No parameters.
- `transparency.disableOpacityMask` (writes): Keeps the opacity masks of the selection or ids but stops applying them. No parameters.
- `transparency.enableOpacityMask` (writes): Applies disabled opacity masks of the selection or ids again. No parameters.
- `transparency.unlinkOpacityMask` (writes): Unlinks the opacity masks of the selection or ids so the objects move without their masks. No parameters.
- `transparency.linkOpacityMask` (writes): Links the opacity masks of the selection or ids again so they move with their objects. No parameters.
- `transparency.toggleNewMasksClipping` (reads): Sets (or toggles) whether new opacity masks clip by default; answers the setting.
  - `value` boolean
- `transparency.toggleNewMasksInverted` (reads): Sets (or toggles) whether new opacity masks are inverted by default; answers the setting.
  - `value` boolean
- `transparency.togglePageIsolatedBlending` (writes): Sets (or toggles) whether the page is an isolated group, so top-level blend modes don't blend with what is under the page; answers the setting.
  - `value` boolean
- `transparency.togglePageKnockoutGroup` (writes): Sets (or toggles) whether the page is a knockout group, so layers hide what they cover; answers the setting.
  - `value` boolean
- `transparency.editOpacityMask` (writes): Enters editing of an object's opacity mask art in place, as clicking its mask thumbnail does.
  - `id` integer or string, an id
- `transparency.stopEditingOpacityMask` (writes): Leaves opacity mask editing and returns to editing the object. No parameters.
- `transparency.viewOpacityMask` (writes): Shows only an object's opacity mask on the canvas as greyscale coverage (or turns that off).
  - `id` integer or string, an id
  - `on` boolean, default: toggle

### Window > Stroke

- `stroke.set` (writes): Sets stroke options of the selection or ids: weight, cap, join, miter limit, alignment, dashes, arrowheads and width profile.
  - `align` string, one of `center` | `inside` | `outside`
  - `alignDashes` boolean, true: dashes fitted to corners and path ends, every run between them holding whole periods with a dash centred on each corner and end; false, the default for a new pattern: exact lengths
  - `arrowAlign` string, one of `extend` | `tip`, tip past the end point, default; tip on the end point; the stroke is shortened
  - `cap` string, one of `butt` | `round` | `square`
  - `dash` array or null
  - `dashOffset` number
  - `endArrow` string or null
  - `ids` array
  - `item` integer or null
  - `join` string, one of `miter` | `round` | `bevel`
  - `miterLimit` number
  - `profile` string or null
  - `startArrow` string or null
  - `weight` number, points

### Window > Appearance

- `appearance.addFill` (writes): Adds a new fill on top of each selected object's appearance stack, copied from its top fill.
  - `ids` array
  - `target` string, one of `object` | `contents`
- `appearance.addStroke` (writes): Adds a new stroke on top of each selected object's appearance stack, copied from its top stroke.
  - `ids` array
  - `target` string, one of `object` | `contents`
- `appearance.clear` (writes): Clears each selected object's appearance to one empty fill and stroke and resets its opacity and blend mode.
  - `ids` array
  - `target` string, one of `object` | `contents`
- `appearance.reduceToBasic` (writes): Keeps only the topmost visible fill and stroke of each selected object and drops extra items and effects.
  - `ids` array
  - `target` string, one of `object` | `contents`
- `appearance.duplicateItem` (writes): Duplicates appearance items (fills or strokes with their effects) in each target's stack, by default right above the original.
  - `ids` array
  - `index` json[], [..] (paint-order item indices); paint-order item indices; one of several alternative parameters
  - `indices` json[], [..] (paint-order item indices); paint-order item indices; one of several alternative parameters
  - `target` string, one of `object` | `contents`
  - `to` integer
- `appearance.showAllHidden` (writes): Makes every hidden fill, stroke and effect of the selected objects visible again; answers the ids changed.
  - `ids` array
  - `target` string, one of `object` | `contents`
- `graphicStyle.redefine` (writes): Replaces a graphic style with the look of object id or the first selected object; every linked object updates.
  - `id` integer or string, an id
  - `name` string
- `appearance.setNewArtBasic` (writes): Sets whether new art gets a basic appearance (one fill and stroke) or the last selected object's whole appearance.
  - `on` boolean, omitted: toggle

### Window > Graphic Styles

- `graphicStyle.apply` (writes): Applies the named graphic style to the selection, ids or a layer, replacing or adding to their appearance.
  - `add` boolean
  - `ids` array, layers too
  - `name` string
  - `target` string, one of `object` | `contents`
- `graphicStyle.new` (writes): Creates a graphic style from object id or the first selected object's appearance and transparency; answers its name.
  - `id` integer or string, an id
  - `name` string
- `graphicStyle.delete` (writes): Deletes graphic styles by name; linked objects keep their look but are unlinked.
  - `name` string
- `graphicStyle.duplicate` (writes): Duplicates a graphic style under a new unique name and answers it.
  - `name` string
- `graphicStyle.breakLink` (writes): Unlinks the selection or ids from their graphic style while keeping their look.
  - `ids` array
- `graphicStyle.rename` (writes): Renames a graphic style; linked objects stay linked.
  - `name` string
  - `to` string
- `graphicStyle.unused` (reads): Answers the names of graphic styles no object is linked to, without changing anything. No parameters.
- `graphicStyle.sortByName` (writes): Sorts the graphic styles by name, keeping the default style first. No parameters.
- `graphicStyle.merge` (writes): Adds a new graphic style combining the fills, strokes and effects of two or more styles; answers its name.
  - `name` string
  - `names` array, two or more
- `graphicStyle.saveLibrary` (writes): Saves the document's graphic styles as a .vcstyles library file, optionally into the user library folder.
  - `name` string
  - `names` json[], [style names] (default: all); default: all
  - `path` file
  - `user` boolean, default `false`, save into the user library folder, listed under User Defined

### Window > Swatches

- `swatch.new` (writes): Adds swatches from a colour, a list of colours, the current fill, a gradient, a pattern or a tint, optionally global or spot and in a group.
  - `global` boolean
  - `group` string
  - `mode` string, one of `gray` | `rgb` | `hsb` | `lab` | `cmyk` | `web`, convert the colour; lab: CIE L*a*b*, how spot colours are usually defined
  - `name` string
  - `spot` boolean
  - `tint` integer, 0 to 100; % of the global or spot `swatch`, or of the one the current fill links to
- `swatch.delete` (writes): Deletes swatches or colour groups by name in one undo step; art using a deleted global swatch keeps its colour unlinked.
  - `name` json[], [swatch or colour group names] (a group goes with its swatches); a group goes with its swatches; one of several alternative parameters
  - `names` json[], [swatch or colour group names] (a group goes with its swatches); a group goes with its swatches; one of several alternative parameters
  - `unlink` boolean, default `true`, art using a deleted global swatch keeps its colour, unlinked; false keeps the stale link
- `swatch.newGroup` (writes): Creates a colour group from existing swatches, new colours or the selected art's colours.
  - `colors` string[], added as new swatches
  - `fromArtwork` boolean, default `false`, add the unique colours of the selected art: fills, strokes, text, gradient stops and mesh points; a colour linked to a global swatch moves that swatch into the group
  - `includeTints` boolean, default `false`, with fromArtwork: tints of global swatches also get swatches of their own
  - `name` string
  - `swatches` json[], [names] (solid colours move into the group; gradients, patterns and None stay); solid colours move into the group; gradients, patterns and None stay
  - `toGlobal` boolean, default `true`, with fromArtwork: the new swatches are global and the selected art's matching unlinked colours link to them
- `swatch.duplicate` (writes): Duplicates a swatch under a new unique name.
  - `name` string
- `swatch.sortByName` (writes): Sorts the swatches by name. No parameters.
- `swatch.edit` (writes): Changes a swatch: its name, colour or colour mode, global and spot flags, or replaces its paint; linked art updates.
  - `color` string, e.g. {l, a, b} for a Lab colour
  - `global` boolean
  - `mode` string, one of `gray` | `rgb` | `hsb` | `lab` | `cmyk` | `web`, convert the colour
  - `name` string
  - `newName` string
  - `paint` object
  - `spot` boolean
- `swatch.move` (writes): Moves swatches (or colour groups) to a position or into another colour group.
  - `group` string
  - `name` array, [swatch names, in order; or colour group names to reorder the groups]; one of several alternative parameters
  - `names` array, [swatch names, in order; or colour group names to reorder the groups]; one of several alternative parameters
  - `to` integer
- `swatch.addUsedColors` (writes): Adds a swatch for each colour the art (or only the selection) uses, optionally global and linking the matching paints.
  - `global` boolean, default `false`, the new swatches are global and the matching unlinked colours in that art link to them
  - `selection` boolean, default `false`, only the selected art's colours; default: all the art's
- `swatch.unused` (reads): Answers the names of swatches nothing in the document uses, without changing anything. No parameters.
- `swatch.merge` (writes): Merges two or more solid swatches into the first; paints linked to the others relink to it.
  - `names` json[], [two or more solid-colour swatches]
- `swatch.ungroup` (writes): Dissolves a colour group, moving its swatches to the ungrouped list; answers their names.
  - `name` string
- `swatch.sortByKind` (writes): Orders the swatches by kind: None, process colours, spot colours, gradients, then patterns. No parameters.
- `swatch.spotOptions` (writes): Sets whether Lab-defined spot colours display and export from their Lab values or their CMYK equivalents.
  - `useLab` boolean, omitted: unchanged
- `swatch.editGroup` (writes): Rewrites a colour group's colours in order (adding or removing swatches as needed) and optionally renames it.
  - `colors` string[], hex, key, {c,m,y,k} or {l,a,b}; the group's swatches take them in order, extra colours become new swatches, swatches past the end are removed; built-in swatches can't change
  - `group` string
  - `rename` string
- `swatch.library.save` (writes): Saves the document's swatches as a library file (native JSON, GPL palette or ASE exchange), or answers the data.
  - `format` string, one of `vcswatches` | `gpl` | `ase` | `css`, lossless JSON: colour models, global, spot, gradients, groups; 8-bit RGB palette; groups as `# Group:` comments; swatch exchange, binary: solid colors in their own model (RGB, CMYK, Lab, Gray) as global, spot or process colors, and color groups; gradients are left out, and a tint swatch is saved as the color it shows; custom properties on :root; default: the path's extension, else vcswatches
  - `name` string
  - `names` json[], [swatch or colour group names] (default: all; None and patterns are never saved); default: all; None and patterns are never saved
  - `path` file
  - `user` boolean, default `false`, save into the user library folder, listed under User Defined

### Window > Gradient

- `paint.editGradient` (writes): Sets or edits the gradient on the fill or stroke of the selection: kind (linear, radial, freeform), stops, angle and aspect.
  - `angle` number, degrees
  - `aspect` number, percent
  - `ids` array
  - `item` integer or null
  - `kind` string, one of `linear` | `radial` | `freeform`, freeform places points on each object, coloured along the stops
  - `mode` string, one of `points` | `lines`, freeform: how the Gradient tool adds points
  - `reverse` boolean
  - `stops` object[], [{offset 0..1, color? (needed without swatch), opacity? 0..1 (or 0..100), midpoint? 0.13..0.87, swatch?: colour swatch name (a global or spot colour or tint swatch links the stop, so swatch edits recolour it and a spot stop prints on its plate; a process colour just gives its colour), tint?: 0..100 (% of the linked swatch; default 100, or a tint swatch's own)}] (at least 2; a freeform gradient's points are recoloured along them); needed without swatch; or 0..100; a global or spot colour or tint swatch links the stop, so swatch edits recolour it and a spot stop prints on its plate; a process colour just gives its colour; % of the linked swatch; default 100, or a tint swatch's own; at least 2; a freeform gradient's points are recoloured along them
  - `stroke` boolean, default: the targeted item's kind, else the active proxy
