  - `strokeMode` string, one of `within` | `along` | `across`, strokes only: the gradient lies on the page and shows through the stroke, runs from the start of each subpath to its end, or runs from the stroke's left edge to its right all along it; with nothing selected, for the next object drawn; type characters' own strokes always paint within

### Window > Layers

- `layer.new` (writes): Adds a layer directly above the current layer (or on top of all layers) with optional name, colour, template, lock, visibility and print options; answers its id.
  - `color` string
  - `dimImages` number or boolean
  - `locked` boolean
  - `name` string
  - `preview` boolean
  - `printable` boolean
  - `template` boolean
  - `top` boolean
  - `visible` boolean
- `layer.newSublayer` (writes): Adds a sublayer on top of a layer's contents (default the current layer); answers its id.
  - `name` string
  - `parent` integer
- `layer.delete` (writes): Deletes Layers panel rows (layers, sublayers, groups or objects) with what they hold; the last layer always stays. No parameters.
- `layer.duplicate` (writes): Duplicates Layers panel rows, each copy just above its original; answers the copies' ids. No parameters.
- `layer.setProps` (writes): Sets layer options on rows: name, visibility, lock, template, printing, preview, image dimming and colour.
  - `color` integer or string
  - `dimImages` number or boolean
  - `id` integer or string, an id; default: the highlighted rows, else the current layer; one of several alternative parameters
  - `ids` array, default: the highlighted rows, else the current layer; one of several alternative parameters
  - `locked` boolean
  - `name` string
  - `preview` boolean
  - `printable` boolean
  - `template` boolean
  - `visible` boolean
- `layer.collectInNew` (writes): Moves the given rows (or the selected objects) into a new layer where the topmost of them was; answers its id.
  - `ids` array
- `layer.clippingMask.toggle` (writes): Makes (or releases) a layer-level clipping mask: the layer's or group's top object clips the rest of it.
  - `id` integer
- `layer.pasteRemembersLayers` (writes): Sets (or toggles) whether pasting puts objects back into the layers they were copied from.
  - `on` boolean
- `layer.merge` (writes): Merges two or more highlighted rows into the last one, keeping stacking order and removing emptied layers; answers its id.
  - `ids` array
- `layer.flatten` (writes): Moves the art of every other visible top-level layer into one layer, deleting hidden layers; template layers stay.
  - `id` integer or string, an id
- `layer.releaseToLayers` (writes): Moves each object of a layer or group into its own new sublayer, in stacking order (build stacks them cumulatively for animation).
  - `build` boolean
  - `id` integer
- `layer.releaseToLayersBuild` (writes): Releases a layer's objects into sublayers that build up cumulatively (each sublayer holds one more object); answers the new ids.
  - `id` integer or string, an id
- `layer.reverse` (writes): Reverses the stacking order of two or more rows that share a layer or group.
  - `ids` array
- `layer.template` (writes): Turns layers into templates (locked, dimmed, left out of print and export) or back into ordinary layers.
  - `ids` array
  - `on` boolean, default: toggle the first
- `layer.hideOthers` (writes): Hides every top-level layer except those holding the highlighted rows (or the current layer).
  - `ids` array
- `layer.showAll` (writes): Shows every layer and sublayer; answers how many changed. No parameters.
- `layer.outlineOthers` (writes): Turns every other top-level layer into outline view, keeping the highlighted ones in preview.
  - `ids` array
- `layer.previewAll` (writes): Turns preview on for every layer and sublayer; answers how many changed. No parameters.
- `layer.lockOthers` (writes): Locks every top-level layer except those holding the highlighted rows (or the current layer).
  - `ids` array
- `layer.unlockAll` (writes): Unlocks every layer and sublayer; answers how many changed. No parameters.
- `layer.locate` (reads): Highlights an object's row in the Layers panel and answers its ancestry of layers; the document is unchanged.
  - `id` integer or string, an id

### Window > Artboards

- `artboard.new` (writes): Adds an artboard at a position and size (default right of the last one) with an optional name.
  - `height` number
  - `name` string
  - `width` number
  - `x` number
  - `y` number
- `artboard.delete` (writes): Deletes the artboard at index; its art stays on the canvas.
  - `index` integer, a position counted from 0 (the first is 0)
- `artboard.setProps` (writes): Changes an artboard's name, position or size, optionally moving or scaling the art inside it.
  - `height` number
  - `index` integer, a position counted from 0 (the first is 0)
  - `moveArt` boolean, default false; a position-only change moves the contained art with its artboard
  - `name` string
  - `scaleArt` boolean, Scale Artwork with Artboard: resized, the artboard takes the art fully inside it (locked and hidden art only with lockedAndHidden?: bool, default prefs moveLockedWithArtboard) and its guides from its old rectangle onto the new one, each side by its own ratio; strokes/corners/patterns as object.scale
  - `width` number
  - `x` number
  - `y` number
- `artboard.duplicate` (writes): Duplicates an artboard to the right of the last one, optionally with copies of the art fully inside it.
  - `art` boolean, default: the Artboard tool's moveArt option
  - `index` integer, default: the Artboard tool's artboard

### Object > Artboards

- `artboard.fitToArt` (writes): Resizes an artboard to the visible art's bounds (strokes and effects included).
  - `index` integer, a position counted from 0 (the first is 0)
- `artboard.fitToSelection` (writes): Resizes an artboard to the bounds of the selected art.
  - `index` integer, a position counted from 0 (the first is 0)
- `artboard.convertToArtboards` (writes): Turns each selected object's bounds into a new artboard, removing the objects. No parameters.
- `artboard.rearrange` (writes): Rearranges all artboards in a grid, row or column with an order, column count and spacing, optionally moving their art.
  - `columns` integer, 2; the rows for gridByColumn; row and column ignore it
  - `layout` string, one of `gridByRow` | `gridByColumn` | `row` | `column`, gridByRow; byColumn?: true is gridByColumn
  - `moveArtwork` boolean, default `true`, locked and hidden art only with prefs moveLockedWithArtboard
  - `order` string, one of `leftToRight` | `rightToLeft`, leftToRight: right-to-left mirrors the order along the rows
  - `spacing` number, points; 20

### Window > Pathfinder

- `object.pathfinder.unite` (writes): Unites the selected shapes into one shape (Pathfinder Unite); answers the resulting ids. No parameters.
- `object.pathfinder.minusFront` (writes): Subtracts the front selected shapes from the backmost one (Pathfinder Minus Front); answers the resulting ids. No parameters.
- `object.pathfinder.intersect` (writes): Keeps only the area where all selected shapes overlap (Pathfinder Intersect); answers the resulting ids. No parameters.
- `object.pathfinder.exclude` (writes): Keeps the areas where the selected shapes don't overlap (Pathfinder Exclude); answers the resulting ids. No parameters.
- `object.pathfinder.divide` (writes): Divides the selected shapes into all the separate faces their overlaps form (Pathfinder Divide); answers the resulting ids. No parameters.
- `object.pathfinder.trim` (writes): Removes the hidden parts of the selected filled shapes without merging same colours (Pathfinder Trim); answers the resulting ids. No parameters.
- `object.pathfinder.merge` (writes): Removes hidden parts and merges touching shapes of the same colour (Pathfinder Merge); answers the resulting ids. No parameters.
- `object.pathfinder.crop` (writes): Crops the selected shapes to the topmost one's outline (Pathfinder Crop); answers the resulting ids. No parameters.
- `object.pathfinder.outline` (writes): Divides the selected shapes into their edge segments as stroked paths (Pathfinder Outline); answers the resulting ids. No parameters.
- `object.pathfinder.minusBack` (writes): Subtracts the back selected shapes from the frontmost one (Pathfinder Minus Back); answers the resulting ids. No parameters.

### Type > Orientation

- `type.orientation.vertical` (writes): Sets the selected or given type objects to vertical writing. No parameters.
- `type.orientation.horizontal` (writes): Sets the selected or given type objects to horizontal writing. No parameters.

### Type

- `type.createOutlines` (writes): Converts the selected text into groups of compound paths, one per glyph; the text is no longer editable. No parameters.
- `text.areaOptions` (writes): Sets area type options of the selected type: frame size, rows, columns, gutter, inset, first baseline, vertical alignment and auto-fit.
  - `columns` integer
  - `firstBaseline` string, one of `ascent` | `capHeight` | `xHeight` | `leading` | `fixed`
  - `firstBaselineMin` number, points
  - `fit` string, one of `none` | `autoHeight` | `shrinkText`
  - `fitMinPercent` integer, 10 to 100
  - `gutter` number, points
  - `height` number, points
  - `ids` array
  - `inset` number, points
  - `rows` integer
  - `verticalAlign` string, one of `top` | `center` | `bottom` | `justify`
  - `width` number, points
- `text.fitHeadline` (writes): Tracks the first line of area type so it fills the frame width; answers the tracking used.
  - `ids` array
- `type.smartPunctuation` (writes): Replaces straight quotes, double hyphens and triple dots with typographic quotes, dashes and ellipses in the selection or document.
  - `dashes` boolean, default `true`, -- → en dash, --- → em dash
  - `ellipsis` boolean, default `true`, ... → …
  - `quotes` boolean, default `true`, straight quotes become the Document Setup quotes
  - `scope` string, one of `selection` | `document`
- `type.convertToAreaType` (writes): Converts point type to area type framed by its current bounds; answers the ids.
  - `ids` array
- `type.convertToPointType` (writes): Converts area type to point type, turning soft wraps into line breaks; answers the ids.
  - `ids` array
- `type.fillPlaceholder` (writes): Replaces the selected text with placeholder text (area type fills its frame).
  - `ids` array
- `type.insert` (writes): Inserts a special character (bullet, dash, quote, space, hyphen or symbol) at the Type tool's caret.
  - `char` string
- `type.fitHeadline` (writes): Tracks the first line of the selected area type so it fills the frame width; answers the tracking.
  - `ids` array
- `text.insertInline` (writes): Inserts a symbol inline into text at a byte offset, scaled and shifted relative to the font size.
  - `at` integer
  - `id` integer
  - `scale` number
  - `shift` number
  - `symbol` string

### Object > Blend

- `object.blend.make` (writes): Blends the selected objects with a number of steps or a distance (or smooth colour) along the page or a path.
  - `ids` array
  - `orientation` string, one of `page` | `path`
  - `starts` array, [anchor index | null, …] (per object of `ids`, else of the selection in paint order: the anchor of its first subpath the blend starts from; an open path's last anchor runs it the other way); per object of `ids`, else of the selection in paint order: the anchor of its first subpath the blend starts from; an open path's last anchor runs it the other way
  - `steps` integer
- `object.blend.release` (writes): Releases the selected blends: the key objects come back and the spine stays as an unpainted path below them. No parameters.
- `object.blend.options` (reads): Sets spacing (smooth, steps or distance) and orientation of the selected blends, or the defaults for new blends when none is selected.
  - `distance` number, points
  - `orientation` string, one of `page` | `path`
  - `spacing` string, one of `smooth` | `steps` | `distance`
  - `steps` integer
  - `value` integer
- `object.blend.expand` (writes): Expands the selected blends into groups of their keys and generated steps; answers the ids. No parameters.
- `object.blend.replaceSpine` (writes): Uses the selected path as the spine of the selected blend; the path is consumed. No parameters.
- `object.blend.reverseSpine` (writes): Reverses the order of the key objects along the selected blend's spine. No parameters.
- `object.blend.reverseFrontToBack` (writes): Reverses the stacking order of the selected blends' steps. No parameters.

### Object > Envelope Distort

- `object.envelope.makeWithWarp` (writes): Wraps the selected objects in a warp envelope of a style (arc, wave, flag, fisheye…) with bend and distortion; answers the envelope's id.
  - `bend` number
  - `h` number
  - `horizontal` boolean
  - `ids` array
  - `style` string, one of `arc` | `arcLower` | `arcUpper` | `arch` | `bulge` | `shellLower` | `shellUpper` | `flag` | `wave` | `fish` | `rise` | `fisheye` | `inflate` | `squeeze` | `twist`, arc
  - `v` number
- `object.envelope.makeWithMesh` (writes): Wraps the selected objects in a mesh envelope of rows by columns patches; answers its id.
  - `cols` integer, 1 to 50; 4
  - `ids` array
  - `rows` integer, 1 to 50; 4
- `object.envelope.makeWithTopObject` (writes): Makes the topmost selected path the envelope of the other selected objects; answers its id.
  - `ids` array
- `object.envelope.resetWithWarp` (writes): Turns the selected envelopes into warp envelopes with a style and bend, keeping their content.
  - `bend` number
  - `h` number
  - `horizontal` boolean
  - `orientation` string, one of `horizontal` | `vertical`
  - `style` string
  - `v` number
- `object.envelope.resetWithMesh` (writes): Turns the selected envelopes into mesh envelopes of rows by columns, keeping their content.
  - `cols` integer, 1 to 50; unset: a mesh envelope's own, else 4
  - `maintainShape` boolean, true: the mesh follows the current envelope shape; false: a flat grid over the content
  - `rows` integer, 1 to 50
- `object.envelope.release` (writes): Releases the selected envelopes into their content and their shape (a mesh or the top path); answers the ids. No parameters.
- `object.envelope.options` (writes): Sets envelope options of the selection: fidelity, anti-aliasing, shape preservation and whether appearance, gradients and patterns distort.
  - `antiAlias` boolean
  - `bend` number
  - `distortAppearance` boolean
  - `distortLinearGradients` boolean
  - `distortPatternFills` boolean, the last two work with distortAppearance
  - `fidelity` integer, 0 to 100
  - `h` number
  - `horizontal` boolean
  - `preserveShape` string, one of `clippingMask` | `transparency`
  - `style` string
  - `v` number
- `object.envelope.expand` (writes): Replaces the selected envelopes with groups of their distorted content (type outlined); answers the ids. No parameters.
- `object.envelope.editContents` (writes): Switches the selected envelopes between editing their contents and editing the envelope itself.
  - `editing` boolean

### View > Proof Setup

- `view.proofSetup` (reads): Sets the soft-proof target (a CMYK profile or a colour-blindness simulation), intent and paper simulation; answers the proof state.
  - `intent` string, one of `perceptual` | `relative` | `saturation` | `absolute`
  - `proof` boolean, also turn Proof Colors on
  - `simulatePaper` boolean
  - `target` string, one of `workingCmyk` | `cmyk:<profile>` | `legacyMacRgb` | `srgb` | `monitorRgb` | `protanopia` | `deuteranopia`

### View

- `view.proofColors` (reads): Turns soft-proofing of colours on, off or toggles it; answers the proof state.
  - `on` boolean, default: toggle
- `view.overprintPreview` (reads): Turns Overprint Preview on, off or toggles it; answers the proof state.
  - `on` boolean, default: toggle
- `view.saved.new` (writes): Saves a named view (centre, zoom, rotation); answers its name and index.
  - `center` number[]
  - `name` string
  - `rotation` number, degrees
  - `zoom` number
- `view.saved.edit` (writes): Renames or deletes a saved view; without params answers the views.
  - `delete` boolean
  - `name` string
  - `newName` string
- `view.transparencyGrid` (reads): Shows, hides or toggles the transparency grid behind the document's artboards; answers the setting.
  - `on` boolean, default: toggle
- `view.slices.hide` (reads): Hides, shows or toggles slices on the canvas (session view state).
  - `hidden` boolean
- `view.slices.lock` (reads): Locks, unlocks or toggles slices so the Slice Selection tool can't change them.
  - `locked` boolean
- `view.printTiling` (reads): Shows, hides or toggles the print pages on the canvas; answers the setting.
  - `on` boolean, default: toggle

### Type > Change Case

- `type.changeCase` (writes): Changes the case of the selected text or ids to upper, lower, title or sentence case.
  - `case` string, one of `upper` | `lower` | `title` | `sentence`
  - `ids` array

### Type > Type on a Path

- `type.pathOptions` (writes): Sets type-on-a-path options: start and end brackets, flip, effect (rainbow, skew, ribbon, stair step, gravity), alignment and spacing.
  - `alignToPath` string, one of `ascender` | `descender` | `center` | `baseline`
  - `effect` string, one of `rainbow` | `skew` | `3dRibbon` | `stairStep` | `gravity`
  - `end` number or null
  - `flip` boolean
  - `ids` array
  - `spacing` number, points
  - `start` number, 0 to 1

### Window > Type > Character Styles

- `charStyle.new` (writes): Creates a character style from attributes or the selected text's; answers its name.
  - `attrs` object
  - `name` string
- `charStyle.redefine` (writes): Redefines a character style from the selected text; text using it updates and keeps its overrides.
  - `id` integer or string, an id
  - `name` string
  - `start` number
- `charStyle.duplicate` (writes): Duplicates a character style under a new name and answers it.
  - `name` string
- `charStyle.delete` (writes): Deletes a character style; text using it keeps its look.
  - `name` string

### Window > Type > Paragraph Styles

- `paraStyle.new` (writes): Creates a paragraph style from attributes or the selected text's; answers its name.
  - `attrs` object
  - `name` string
- `paraStyle.redefine` (writes): Redefines a paragraph style from the selected text; paragraphs using it update.
  - `id` integer or string, an id
  - `name` string
  - `start` number
- `paraStyle.duplicate` (writes): Duplicates a paragraph style under a new name and answers it.
  - `name` string
- `paraStyle.delete` (writes): Deletes a paragraph style; text using it keeps its look.
  - `name` string

### Type > Threaded Text

- `text.thread.create` (writes): Threads the selected area type and closed paths in stacking order so text flows from one frame to the next; answers the ids. No parameters.
- `text.thread.releaseSelection` (writes): Takes the selected frames out of their threads; the story reflows through the rest. No parameters.
- `text.thread.remove` (writes): Breaks the selected frames' threads, each frame keeping the text it shows. No parameters.

### Object > Text Wrap

- `object.textWrap.make` (writes): Makes area type below the selected objects wrap around them with an offset; answers the ids.
  - `ids` array
  - `invert` boolean
  - `offset` number, points; 6
- `object.textWrap.release` (writes): Stops the selected objects from making text wrap around them; answers the ids.
  - `ids` array
- `object.textWrap.options` (writes): Sets the offset and inversion of the selected text-wrap objects, or answers the current options.
  - `ids` array
  - `invert` boolean
  - `offset` number, points

### Object > Graph

- `graph.setData` (writes): Replaces a graph's data from series, categories and rows or CSV; without data answers the current data.
  - `categories` string[]
  - `csv` string
  - `id` integer or string, an id
  - `rows` integer
  - `series` string[]
- `graph.setType` (writes): Changes a graph's type and options: column and cluster width, legend, markers, axes ranges, ticks and labels.
  - `axisMax` number
  - `axisMin` number
  - `categoryTickLength` string, one of `none` | `short` | `full`
  - `categoryTickMarks` integer
  - `clusterWidth` number, percent
  - `columnWidth` number, percent
  - `connectPoints` boolean
  - `edgeToEdge` boolean, line graphs: true runs the lines across the whole plot, false puts the points at the centres of their categories
  - `id` integer or string, an id
  - `legend` boolean
  - `markPoints` boolean
  - `prefix` string
  - `rightAxisMax` number
  - `rightAxisMin` number
  - `rightPrefix` string
  - `rightSuffix` string
  - `rightTickLength` string, one of `none` | `short` | `full`
  - `rightTickMarks` integer
  - `rightTicks` integer
  - `separateScales` boolean
  - `seriesIndexes` integer[]
  - `suffix` string
  - `tickLength` string, one of `none` | `short` | `full`
  - `tickMarks` integer
  - `ticks` integer
  - `ticksBetweenLabels` boolean
  - `type` string, one of `column` | `stackedColumn` | `bar` | `stackedBar` | `line` | `area` | `scatter` | `pie` | `radar`
  - `valueAxis` string, one of `left` | `right` | `both`, the bar graphs' value axis stays along the bottom

### Effect

- `document.rasterEffectsSettings` (writes): Sets the document's raster effects settings: resolution, colour model, background, anti-aliasing and clipping mask.
  - `addAround` number, points; 0–1000, room around the art
  - `antiAlias` boolean, off: hard edges
  - `background` string, one of `transparent` | `white`
  - `clippingMask` boolean, white background only under the art; Rasterize clips to the art
  - `colorModel` string, one of `rgb` | `cmyk` | `grayscale` | `bitmap`, the document's mode
  - `preserveSpotColors` boolean, stored
  - `resolution` number or string

### Window > Tabs

- `text.tabs.set` (writes): Replaces the tab stops of the selected text's paragraphs with positions, alignments and leaders.
  - `end` integer, 0 to 255
  - `ids` array
  - `start` integer, 0 to 255
  - `stops` object[]
- `text.tabs.clear` (writes): Removes all tab stops from the selected text's paragraphs.
  - `end` integer, 0 to 255
  - `ids` array
  - `start` integer, 0 to 255

### View > Guides

- `view.guides.make` (writes): Turns the selected paths into guides; answers how many. No parameters.
- `view.guides.release` (writes): Turns the selected guides (or all guide paths) back into ordinary paths; answers how many. No parameters.
- `view.guides.lock` (reads): Locks, unlocks or toggles guides for the session; answers the lock state.
  - `locked` boolean
- `view.guides.clear` (writes): Deletes all ruler guides and guide paths; answers how many. No parameters.

### File > Document Color Mode

- `file.documentColorMode` (writes): Switches the document between CMYK and RGB, converting every colour, symbol, pattern and swatch through the colour settings.
  - `convert` boolean, default `true`, convert every colour of the art, symbols, pattern tiles and swatches through the colour settings; swatch links kept; Gray colours stay Gray, on the black plate
  - `grays` string, one of `profile` | `black`, default: RGB greys separate through the CMYK profile like any colour, into four-colour greys and a rich black; to CMYK, RGB greys with R = G = B go on the black plate only, K = their grey value
  - `intent` string, one of `perceptual` | `relative` | `saturation` | `absolute`
  - `mode` string, one of `cmyk` | `rgb`

### Window > Variables

- `variable.define` (writes): Defines a text or visibility variable for data-driven graphics.
  - `kind` string, one of `text` | `visibility`
  - `name` string
- `variable.delete` (writes): Deletes variables with their bindings and dataset values (default the highlighted one).
  - `names` string[]
- `variable.rename` (writes): Renames a variable along with its bindings and dataset values.
  - `name` string
  - `newName` string
- `variable.makeTextDynamic` (writes): Defines a text variable over the selected type, named after it and bound to it. No parameters.
- `variable.makeVisibilityDynamic` (writes): Defines a visibility variable over the selection, named after it and bound to it. No parameters.
- `variable.bind` (writes): Binds objects (default the selection) to a variable; text variables need type.
  - `ids` array
  - `variable` string
- `variable.unbind` (writes): Removes variable bindings from objects (default the selection): one variable or all of them.
  - `ids` array
  - `variable` string
- `dataset.new` (writes): Adds a dataset with values per variable.
  - `name` string
  - `values` object
- `dataset.set` (writes): Replaces a dataset's values; variables left out lose their value in it.
  - `name` string
  - `values` object
- `dataset.rename` (writes): Renames a dataset, keeping its values.
  - `name` string
  - `newName` string
- `dataset.capture` (writes): Records what the bound objects hold now as a new dataset and makes it active.
  - `name` string
- `dataset.update` (writes): Writes what the bound objects hold now into the active dataset. No parameters.
- `dataset.delete` (writes): Deletes datasets (default the active one).
  - `names` string[]
- `dataset.select` (writes): Applies a dataset's values to the bound objects in one undo step; answers what was applied and skipped.
  - `name` string
- `dataset.next` (writes): Applies the next dataset, wrapping around. No parameters.
- `dataset.prev` (writes): Applies the previous dataset, wrapping around. No parameters.

### Window > Document Info

- `document.info` (reads): Answers the Document Info report: objects, styles, swatches, patterns, gradients, symbols, fonts and images, for the document or the selection.
  - `category` string, one of `document` | `objects` | `graphicStyles` | `spotColors` | `patterns` | `gradients` | `symbols` | `fonts` | `fontDetails` | `linkedImages` | `embeddedImages`, only that one in sections and the text
  - `format` string, like text; → {text}: the report Document Info › Save… and Package write
  - `selectionOnly` boolean

### Object > Region Paint

- `livePaint.make` (writes): Builds a Region Paint group from the selected paths so faces and edges can be painted; answers its id and counts.
  - `ids` array
- `livePaint.merge` (writes): Adds the other selected paths and groups to the first Region Paint group, keeping its paint.
  - `ids` array
- `livePaint.release` (writes): Replaces Region Paint groups with their original paths.
  - `id` integer or string, an id
- `livePaint.expand` (writes): Turns Region Paint groups into plain groups of their painted faces and edges.
  - `id` integer or string, an id

### Object > Image Trace

- `imageTrace.make` (writes): Traces an embedded image into vector paths with a preset or parameters (mode, threshold, colours, paths, corners, noise); the result stays live.
  - `id` integer
  - `params` object, {mode: "blackAndWhite"|"grayscale"|"color"|"logo", threshold: 0-255, palette: "limited"|"fullTone"|"automatic"|"documentLibrary" (color mode; limited: the `colors` best colours, fullTone: as many as the tones need, more with colorDetail, automatic: flat art with its own colours, else fullTone, documentLibrary: at most `colors` of the library's colours, as they are), colors: 2-256, colorDetail: 0-100 (fullTone, automatic), library: "document" (the document's swatches) or a swatch library id or name (swatch.library.list; documentLibrary), paths: 0-100, corners: 0-100, noise: px, method: "abutting"|"overlapping", ignoreWhite, snapCurvesToLines, fills: true, strokes: false (Create: lines up to strokeWidth wide become stroked centre lines; without fills, wider areas become stroked outlines), strokeWidth: px (10), logoColors?: ["#rrggbb"…] (mode logo: flat-colour logos only; colours found automatically or named here, white is always its own colour, at most ten; noise = areas under noise/10 px ignored; edges to a fraction of a pixel, sharp corners restored, lines and circles snapped; enclosed transparent areas are painted white unless ignoreWhite makes them holes; fills/strokes are ignored; gradients and photos are refused)}; color mode; limited: the `colors` best colours, fullTone: as many as the tones need, more with colorDetail, automatic: flat art with its own colours, else fullTone, documentLibrary: at most `colors` of the library's colours, as they are; fullTone, automatic; the document's swatches; swatch.library.list; documentLibrary; Create: lines up to strokeWidth wide become stroked centre lines; without fills, wider areas become stroked outlines; 10; mode logo: flat-colour logos only; colours found automatically or named here, white is always its own colour, at most ten; noise = areas under noise/10 px ignored; edges to a fraction of a pixel, sharp corners restored, lines and circles snapped; enclosed transparent areas are painted white unless ignoreWhite makes them holes; fills/strokes are ignored; gradients and photos are refused
  - `preset` string, imageTrace.presets
  - `view` string, one of `tracingResult` | `tracingResultWithOutlines` | `outlines` | `outlinesWithSourceImage` | `sourceImage`
- `imageTrace.makeAndExpand` (writes): Traces an image like imageTrace.make and expands the result into plain paths; answers the counts. No parameters.
- `imageTrace.release` (writes): Puts the source image back in place of Image Trace groups.
  - `id` integer or string, an id
- `imageTrace.expand` (writes): Keeps only the traced paths of Image Trace groups, dropping the source image.
  - `id` integer or string, an id

### Object > Shaper

- `shaper.release` (writes): Releases a Shaper group back to its original paths.
  - `id` integer or string, an id; default: selection
- `shaper.expand` (writes): Expands a Shaper group into ordinary paths of its visible result.
  - `id` integer or string, an id; default: selection

### Object > Pattern

- `object.pattern.make` (writes): Makes a pattern swatch from the selection with a tile type and size, and enters pattern editing mode; answers its name.
  - `brickOffset` number, 0 to 1; 0.5
  - `edit` boolean, true
  - `height` number
  - `ids` array
  - `name` string
  - `tileType` string, one of `grid` | `brickByRow` | `brickByColumn` | `hexByColumn` | `hexByRow`
  - `width` number
- `object.pattern.edit` (writes): Enters pattern editing mode for a pattern (default the selected object's fill pattern).
  - `name` string

### Window > Pattern Options

- `pattern.options` (writes): Sets a pattern's options: name, tile type, brick offset, size, spacing, overlap and editing display.
  - `brickOffset` number
  - `copies` integer, one of `3` | `5` | `7` | `9`
  - `dimCopies` number, percent
  - `hSpacing` number
  - `height` number
  - `name` string, default: the pattern being edited
  - `newName` string
  - `overlap` object
  - `showSwatchBounds` boolean, outline the part of the tiling the swatch repeats, dashed
  - `showTileEdge` boolean
  - `sizeTileToArt` boolean
  - `tileType` string, one of `grid` | `brickByRow` | `brickByColumn` | `hexByColumn` | `hexByRow`
  - `vSpacing` number
  - `width` number

### Object > Repeat

- `object.repeat.radial` (writes): Makes a radial repeat of the selection with a number of instances and radius; answers its id.
  - `ids` array
  - `instances` integer, 8
  - `radius` number, points
- `object.repeat.grid` (writes): Makes a grid repeat of the selection with rows, columns and spacing; answers its id.
  - `cols` integer, 3
  - `hSpacing` number, points
  - `ids` array
  - `rows` integer, 3
  - `vSpacing` number, points; ¼ of the art size
- `object.repeat.mirror` (writes): Makes a mirror repeat of the selection about an axis angle and offset; answers its id.
  - `angle` number, degrees; 90 = vertical axis
  - `ids` array
  - `offset` number, points; 10
- `object.repeat.release` (writes): Releases the selected repeats back to their source art. No parameters.
- `object.repeat.options` (writes): Sets the options of the selected repeats (radial instances and angles, grid spacing and flips, mirror angle).
  - `center` number[]
  - `cols` integer
  - `endAngle` number
  - `flipRows` boolean
  - `gridType` string
  - `instances` integer
  - `radius` number
  - `reverseOverlap` boolean
  - `rows` integer
  - `startAngle` number
  - `vSpacing` number

### Window > Swatch Libraries

- `swatch.library.add` (writes): Adds swatches or colour groups from a library to the document's swatches, optionally applying the first to the selection.
  - `apply` string, one of `fill` | `stroke`, also apply the first one to the selection and the defaults, as paint.setFill / paint.setStroke
  - `focus` boolean, default `true`, with apply: false keeps the active proxy
  - `library` string
  - `names` json[], [swatch or colour group names in the library] (default: all of it; a group comes as a colour group, a single swatch ungrouped); default: all of it; a group comes as a colour group, a single swatch ungrouped
- `swatch.resetDefaults` (writes): Restores the default swatches and colour groups of the document's colour mode that are missing, or replaces all swatches with the defaults.
  - `replace` boolean, default `false`
- `swatch.library.load` (writes): Loads a swatch library file (.vcswatches, .gpl, .ase, .acb) or another document's swatches so the library panel lists it.
  - `name` string
- `swatch.library.copyToUser` (writes): Copies a loaded swatch library into the user library folder so it is listed every time the app starts.
  - `library` string

### Window > Graphic Style Libraries

- `graphicStyle.addFromLibrary` (writes): Adds graphic styles from a library to the document, optionally applying the first to the selection.
  - `add` boolean, default `false`, with apply: add its appearance on top, as Alt-click
  - `apply` boolean, default `false`, also apply the first one to `ids` or the selection, if any, as graphicStyle.apply
  - `ids` array
  - `library` string
  - `name` json[], [style names in the library] (default: all of it); default: all of it; one of several alternative parameters
  - `names` json[], [style names in the library] (default: all of it); default: all of it; one of several alternative parameters
- `graphicStyle.loadLibrary` (writes): Loads a .vcstyles library or another document's graphic styles so the library panel lists it.
  - `name` string

### Window > Color Themes

- `colorTheme.save` (writes): Saves a colour theme of 1 to 5 colours (or one made from a colour and a harmony rule), optionally replacing a saved theme.
  - `colors` string[]
  - `name` string, default "Theme N"
  - `replace` string
  - `rule` string
- `colorTheme.delete` (writes): Deletes a saved colour theme.
  - `name` string
- `colorTheme.addToSwatches` (writes): Adds a saved theme's colours to the swatches as a colour group named after it.
  - `name` string

### Object > Slice

- `object.slice.make` (writes): Makes each selected object an object slice that follows its bounds.
  - `ids` array
- `object.slice.release` (writes): Releases the selected slices (object slices leave their object; user slices become unpainted rectangles). No parameters.
- `object.slice.fromGuides` (writes): Replaces the user slices with the grid the ruler guides cut the artboards into. No parameters.
- `object.slice.fromSelection` (writes): Creates a user slice over the visual bounds of the selected objects.
  - `ids` array
- `object.slice.duplicate` (writes): Duplicates the selected slices as user slices, offset by dx, dy.
  - `dx` number, points; default 10
  - `dy` number, points; default 10
- `object.slice.combine` (writes): Combines two or more selected slices into one user slice over their bounds. No parameters.
- `object.slice.divide` (writes): Divides each selected slice into a grid of user slices by count or size.
  - `columnWidth` number
  - `columns` integer
  - `rowHeight` number
  - `rows` integer
- `object.slice.deleteAll` (writes): Deletes every user slice and releases every object slice. No parameters.
- `object.slice.options` (writes): Sets the selected slices' web options: kind, name, URL, target, message, alt text, cell text, background and alignment.
  - `alt` string
  - `background` string, one of `` | `matte` | `#rrggbb`
  - `hAlign` string, one of `default` | `left` | `center` | `right`
  - `kind` string, one of `image` | `noImage` | `htmlText`, object slices of type only
  - `message` string
  - `name` string
  - `target` string
  - `text` string
  - `url` string
  - `vAlign` string, one of `default` | `top` | `middle` | `baseline` | `bottom`
- `object.slice.clipToArtboard` (writes): Sets or toggles whether slices are clipped to the artboards.
  - `on` boolean

### Object > Collect for Export

- `assets.add` (writes): Collects the selected art as assets for asset export, one per object or one for all; answers the assets.
  - `ids` array, default: the selected objects
  - `multiple` boolean, default `true`, an asset per object; false: one asset of them all
  - `name` string, the asset's name, when it makes one

### Object > Plug-ins

- `plugin.reload` (reads): Installs every plug-in module in a folder (default the Additional Plug-ins Folder), reporting failures.
  - `path` file, a folder (default: the Additional Plug-ins Folder preference); default: the Additional Plug-ins Folder preference

## Examples

From [`agent/guide.md`](../agent/guide.md).

### Example 1: a badge with centred type

```json
vector_run {"path": "Badge.kvector", "steps": [
  {"command": "shape.rectangle", "params": {"x": 10, "y": 10, "width": 180, "height": 80, "radius": 12}},
  {"command": "text.create", "params": {"x": 100, "y": 58, "text": "Kition", "size": 28, "color": "#ffffff"}}
]}
```

Answer: `completed: [{command: "shape.rectangle", result: {id: 4}}, {command: "text.create",
result: {id: 5}}]`. Use those ids:

```json
vector_run {"path": "Badge.kvector", "steps": [
  {"command": "select.set", "params": {"ids": [4]}},
  {"command": "paint.setFill", "params": {"color": "#5645d4"}},
  {"command": "select.set", "params": {"ids": [5]}},
  {"command": "object.align", "params": {"horizontal": "center", "vertical": "center", "to": "artboard"}}
]}
vector_check {"path": "Badge.kvector"}
```

The check answers `{"diagnostics": []}`; `vector_inspect {path, preview: true}` shows the purple
badge with the word centred on the artboard.

### Example 2: fixing what the check finds

```json
vector_check {"path": "Poster.kvector"}
```

```json
{"diagnostics": [{"code": "vector.off-artboard", "severity": "warning",
  "target": {"path": "object:4"},
  "message": "Object 4 lies outside every artboard, so exports and prints leave it out."}]}
```

No `fix` is given, so move the object yourself (its bounds are in `vector_inspect`):

```json
vector_run {"path": "Poster.kvector", "steps": [
  {"command": "select.set", "params": {"ids": [4]}},
  {"command": "object.move", "params": {"dx": -560, "dy": 40}}
]}
```

A diagnostic with a fix is applied as given:

```json
vector_check {"path": "Icons.kvector"}
→ {"diagnostics": [{"code": "vector.empty-group", "severity": "info", "target": {"path": "object:1004"},
    "fix": {"command": "edit.clear", "params": {"ids": [1004]}}}]}
vector_run {"path": "Icons.kvector", "steps": [{"command": "edit.clear", "params": {"ids": [1004]}}]}
vector_check {"path": "Icons.kvector"}
→ {"diagnostics": []}
```
